tasks.title: the driver re-runs the acceptance checks at the committed rev: `checks_verified`, `checks_scope`, the total demotion table, the verification budget
tasks.commit_subject: seat: the driver re-runs the acceptance checks at the committed rev — checks_verified, checks_scope, the total demotion table, the verification budget (test: unit, evidence-unit, lint)
tasks.body:
**Files:**
- Create: `tests/evidence/fixtures/results/checks.result`
- Modify: `tools/factory/seat/factory-task`, `tools/factory/seat/factory-lib.sh`, `pkgs/evidence/streams.py`, `pkgs/evidence/ingest_result.py`, `pkgs/evidence/SCHEMA.md`, `tests/evidence/test_streams_policy.py`, `tests/evidence/test_ingest_result.py`, `tests/unit/94-seat-harness.bats`, `tests/unit/80-seat-driver.bats` (the `factory_error_class` precedence test gains rows), `tools/factory/seat/README.md`

**Interfaces:**

- Environment: `FACTORY_VERIFY_TIMEOUT` (seconds, default 1800) — one budget per task shared by every driver verification (this task's checks, SH5's probes); outside `FACTORY_TIMEOUT` (the seat's own bound). `FACTORY_VERIFY=0` skips verification entirely (an operator hand run): no `checks_verified:` line is written and the log says `verify: skipped (FACTORY_VERIFY=0)` — the record then carries the seat's unverified line, labelled by absence.
- `factory-lib.sh`:
  - `factory_record_check <name> <rev> ok|fail <duration_s> [<src>]`: a fifth argument, default `seat-integrate` (the integrator's calls are unchanged); this task records with `seat-verify`.
  - `factory_latest_check <name> <rev>`: `"$FACTORY_EVIDENCE_CMD"` when set, else `factory_python3 …/evidence.py`, with `${EVIDENCE_STORE:+--store "$EVIDENCE_STORE"} latest-check --name "$name" --rev "$rev"`; prints the row and returns 0 when one exists, 1 otherwise (never fails the caller).
  - `factory_acceptance_names <plan> <KEY>`: the `**acceptance:**` line of `factory_extract_task`'s section, split on commas and whitespace, one per line — the section's own line, never the commit subject's `(test: …)` and never the seat's `FACTORY-CHECKS`. Empty when there is no section or no line.
  - `factory_flake_checks <ws> <rev>`: `nix eval --json "git+file://$ws?ref=$rev#checks.x86_64-linux" --apply builtins.attrNames`, one name per line; returns 1 and prints nothing when the evaluation fails (its last 200 bytes logged) — the caller then marks every name `fail` (a rev whose flake does not evaluate has no green check).
  - `factory_check_deferred <ws> <rev> <name> <toplevel-drv>`: 0 when `nix derivation show "git+file://$ws?ref=$rev#checks.x86_64-linux.$name"` shows `"requiredSystemFeatures"` containing `"kvm"` or a `drvPath` equal to `<toplevel-drv>` (the host closure: `nix eval --raw "git+file://$ws?ref=$rev#nixosConfigurations.core.config.system.build.toplevel.drvPath"`, computed once per task, empty when the flake has no such attribute); a deferred check with a `nix build --dry-run` that reports nothing to build (no line ending `will be built:`) is not deferred (a store hit builds instantly).
  - `factory_verify_checks <ws> <rev> <budget-s> <name>…` prints one line per name: `<name> <verdict> <src> <duration_s>` with `verdict` ∈ `pass|fail|not-run:absent|not-run:cache-miss|not-run:verify-timeout` and `src` ∈ `recorded|run|eval|-`. Per name, in order: (1) `factory_latest_check` finds a row at `<rev>` → `pass`/`fail` from its `"ok"`, src `recorded`, nothing run; (2) the name is not in `factory_flake_checks` → `not-run:absent`; the eval failed → `fail`, src `eval`; (3) `factory_check_deferred` → `not-run:cache-miss`; (4) `timeout -- <remaining> nix build "git+file://$ws?ref=$rev#checks.x86_64-linux.$name" --no-link` → exit 0 `pass`, 124 `not-run:verify-timeout` (and every later name is `not-run:verify-timeout` without running; the function returns 3), other `fail`; src `run`; each run verdict is recorded with `factory_record_check <name> <rev> ok|fail <dur> seat-verify`. `<remaining>` is the budget minus the time spent since the first verification began; the caller passes the budget file SH5 reuses.
- `factory-task`, between the extraction of the seat's lines and the synthesis arms (so SH2's `unreported` arm reads the driver's verdicts): when `FACTORY_VERIFY` is not `0` and `head_sha` is not `unknown`: the name set = `factory_acceptance_names` ∪ every `<name>` whose seat token is `pass` in `checks_line` (the seat's claimed passes are verified too; hr1/H2's `pre-commit=pass`); `checks_verified_out=$(factory_verify_checks "$ws" "$head_sha" "$budget" …)`; `verify_s` = the wall of the whole loop. `.result` lines after `touches_*`: `checks_verified: <name>=<verdict> …` (the section's order, claimed-only names after), `checks_verified_src: <name>=<src> …`, `verify_s: <int>`, `checks_scope: clean|dirty`, `checks_scope_files: <n>`, and when dirty `checks_scope_list: <paths>`. `checks_scope` is `dirty` when any path of `git diff --name-only "$base_sha..task/$key"` is `flake.nix` or is covered (the SH3 `/`-boundary rule) by `tests` or `githooks`. SH2's `unreported` arm now sets `checks_line="FACTORY-CHECKS <name>=<v> …"` from `checks_verified` with every `not-run:*` folded to `not-run` (`none=not-run` only when the set is empty).
- **The demotion table** (applied only to a status still `done` after CR3r; `claimed` is the seat's token for the name — `absent` when the name is not on the line or the line is unparseable):

| claimed \ driver | `pass` | `fail` | `not-run:absent` | `not-run:cache-miss` | `not-run:verify-timeout` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pass` | stands | `partial`, `checks-misreported` | `partial`, `checks-unverifiable` | stands (recorded) | stands (recorded) |
| `fail` | stands (recorded) | stands (an honest fail; pa8/P5) | stands | stands | stands |
| `not-run` | stands | `partial`, `checks-misreported` (a `done` over a red acceptance check) | stands | stands | stands |
| absent | stands | `partial`, `checks-misreported` | stands (a plan defect `check --draft` refuses upstream) | stands | stands |

  Several cells firing: `checks-misreported` outranks `checks-unverifiable` (D5); every firing cell appends `; <name> claimed <token>, driver <verdict>` to `FACTORY-NOTES`; `demoted=checks-misreported|checks-unverifiable` and the `status=` field is rewritten in place (the CR3r shape). SH3's `touches` demotion runs after this table and only on a still-`done` status; its arm is outranked, its clause still appended.
- `factory_error_class <log> <status> <exit_code> <wall_s> <events> <synth> <demoted> [<verify>]`: the `case $demoted` gains `checks-misreported) … ;;` and `checks-unverifiable) … ;;` printing the same words, beside `touches`; the optional eighth argument `verify` = `timeout` makes the function print `verify-timeout` wherever it would otherwise print `none` — both in the `done` guard and at the end — and nowhere else.
- `streams.py`: `ERROR_CLASSES` gains `checks-misreported`, `checks-unverifiable`, `verify-timeout` (before `none`, after `touches-violation`); `task-result` gains `"checks_verified": ("null", ("map", ("re", r"^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$"), 64, ("enum", ("pass", "fail", "not-run:absent", "not-run:cache-miss", "not-run:verify-timeout"))))`, `"checks_scope": ("null", ("enum", ("clean", "dirty")))`, `"checks_scope_files": ("null", "int")`, `"verify_s": ("null", "int")`.
- `ingest_result.py`: `checks_verified` ← the line's tokens through a `_parse_verified` that accepts the five verdicts (any violation → `None`, never a partial map); `checks_scope` ← the word when in the enum else `None`; `checks_scope_files`, `verify_s` ← `_as_int`. `checks_verified_src` and `checks_scope_list` are never ingested.
- Consumers: SH2's arm (`FACTORY-CHECKS` for `unreported`), the gate (`checks_scope_list` names the files that define the checks), SH6.

**Facts:**

- `sed -n '82,99p' tools/factory/seat/factory-lib.sh` → `factory_record_check() {` / `local name=$1 rev=$2 verdict=$3 dur=$4 flag` … `record-check --name "$name" --rev "$rev" "$flag" --class nix-check --src seat-integrate --duration "$dur"` — the src is a literal today.
- `sed -n '162,174p' tools/factory/seat/factory-integrate` → `while IFS= read -r chk; do` … `if nix build "git+file://$base?ref=integ/$run#checks.x86_64-linux.$chk" -L --no-link >>"$log" 2>&1; then` / `logboth "CHECK $chk pass"` / `factory_record_check "$chk" "$head" ok "$(( $(date +%s) - t0 ))"` — the `git+file://…?ref=` form that builds the committed rev, never the working tree; `sed -n '130,136p'` → `checks_raw=$(` / `git -C "$base" log --no-merges --pretty=%s "origin/$default_branch..integ/$run" \` / `| grep -oE '\(test: [^)]*\)'` — the subject-derived names this task never uses.

- `sed -n '251,265p' pkgs/evidence/evidence.py` → `def latest_check(store: str, name: str, rev: str) -> dict | None:` … `if r.get("kind") == "check" and r.get("name") == name and r.get("rev") == rev` … `if best is None or r["ts"] >= best["ts"]:` / `best = r` / `return best` (newest wins; a later-appended row wins a one-second tie); the CLI `latest-check --name N --rev SHA` exits 0 with the row, 1 when none (`tests/evidence/test_evidence.py::test_cli_latest_check_exit_codes`).

**Files:**
- Create: `tests/evidence/fixtures/results/probes.result`
- Modify: `pkgs/evidence/tasks.py`, `tests/evidence/test_tasks.py`, `tools/factory/seat/factory-task`, `tools/factory/seat/factory-lib.sh`, `tools/factory/seat/factory-brief`, `pkgs/evidence/streams.py`, `pkgs/evidence/ingest_result.py`, `pkgs/evidence/SCHEMA.md`, `tests/evidence/test_streams_policy.py`, `tests/evidence/test_ingest_result.py`, `tests/unit/94-seat-harness.bats`, `tools/factory/seat/README.md`

**Interfaces:**

- **The section grammar** (read by `parse_plan`): a line `**probes:**` followed immediately by one or more lines `- <name>: `<command>` :: <op>[ <value>] :: <provenance>`; the block ends at the first line that does not start with `- `. `name` matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$` and is unique in the section; `command` is the text between the first and last backtick of the line, may not contain a tab; `op` ∈ `le lt ge gt eq ne empty nonempty`; `value` is required for the first six and forbidden for the last two — for `le lt ge gt` it must parse as a decimal number, for `eq ne` it is any non-space string that does **not** parse as a number (a bare equality on a measured number is refused by the grammar: state a bound); `provenance` is non-empty text (who measured the bound, when, in what environment). A line `**probe_env:** NAME=VALUE …` (each token `^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*=[^ ]*$`) is the section's environment override. `FIELD_RE` gains `probe_env`; `parse_plan` gives every task `"probes": [ {"name","cmd","op","value","by"} … ]` and `"probe_env": "<the line's value>" | None`.
- `tasks.py check` (the draft rules and `check` alike): `tasks: <key> probes: malformed: <line>`, `tasks: <key> probes: duplicate <name>`, `tasks: <key> probes: <name>: op <op> needs a numeric value`, `tasks: <key> probes: <name>: op <op> takes no value`, `tasks: <key> probes: <name>: eq/ne on a number — state a bound (le, ge)`, `tasks: <key> probe_env: malformed token <tok>`.
- `tasks.py probes <plan> <KEY>`: line 1 `env\t<probe_env or empty>`, then one line per probe `<name>\t<op>\t<value>\t<provenance>\t<command>` (tab-separated; the command last); exit 0 with only the env line when the section names no probe; exit 3 with `tasks: probes: no section <KEY> in <plan>` when there is none; exit 2 when the plan is unreadable. Reads the plan file only.
- `factory-brief`, the RULES bullet that introduces the template, gains one sentence before "The first line is exactly the result line": `Before those four lines, print one line `FACTORY-PROBE <name>=<value>` per probe the task section names (none when it names none), the value being your own run's last output line.` — the sentence carries no literal `FACTORY-RESULT`; the four-line template is unchanged (SH2's tests keep counting four).
- `factory-lib.sh`:
  - `factory_task_probes <plan> <KEY>`: `factory_py …/tasks.py probes "$plan" "$key"`; prints its stdout; a non-zero status → "no probes" (logged `probes: no contract for <KEY> (…)`).
  - `factory_probe_compare <op> <bound> <value>`: prints `pass` or `fail`. Numeric ops compare `<value>` as a decimal (a non-numeric value → `fail`); `eq`/`ne` compare the trimmed strings; `empty` passes on an empty value, `nonempty` on a non-empty one.
  - `factory_run_probe <ws> <env-tokens> <remaining-s> <command>`: `cd <ws> && timeout -- <remaining> env -u FACTORY_RUN <env-tokens> bash -c "$command"`, stdout to a temp file, stderr to the task log; prints the last non-empty line of stdout, trimmed, truncated to 200 bytes, control bytes folded to a space; returns 124 on the timeout, else 0 (the command's own exit status is not the verdict — the value is).
- `factory-task`, inside the verification block after SH4's checks (the same budget): `probe_lines` = every log line matching `^FACTORY-PROBE[[:space:]]+[a-z][a-z0-9-]*=` without `<`, the last per name (the seat's values). For each section probe: run it (`FACTORY_RUN` is unset in the probe's environment; the section's `probe_env` tokens applied after; the seat's cwd and rev — the workspace as the seat left it); outcome, in this precedence: `not-run` when the budget is exhausted before it starts or the run returns 124; `fail` when the driver's value fails the bound; `missing` when the driver's value passes and the seat pasted no line for the name; `drift` when both exist and pass but differ as strings; `pass` when the seat's value equals the driver's and passes. `.result` lines after `checks_scope_*`: `probes_verified: <name>=<outcome> …`, `probe_values: <name>=<driver value>|<seat value or ->  …` (values with spaces replaced by `_`; the gate reads it; not ingested), `probe_env: <the env line or ->`. Demotion, on a status still `done` after SH4's table and before SH3's `touches` arm — no: after it (D5): any `fail` → `partial`, `demoted=probe-mismatch`, notes `; probe <name> driver <value> <op> <bound>: fail`; else any `missing` → `partial`, `demoted=probe-missing`, notes `; probe <name> not pasted by the seat`; `drift` and `not-run` append a clause and never demote. D5's full order: `checks-misreported` > `checks-unverifiable` > `touches-violation` > `probe-mismatch` > `probe-missing`.
- `factory_error_class`: `case $demoted` gains `probe-mismatch)` and `probe-missing)` printing the same words.
- `streams.py`: `ERROR_CLASSES` gains `probe-mismatch`, `probe-missing` (after `verify-timeout`, before `none`); `task-result` gains `"probes_verified": ("null", ("map", ("re", r"^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$"), 32, ("enum", ("pass", "fail", "missing", "not-run", "drift"))))`.
- `ingest_result.py`: `probes_verified` ← the line's tokens (any violation → `None`); `probe_values` and `probe_env` are never ingested.
- Consumers: the gate (`probe_values` beside the bound the section states), SH6.

**Files:** - Modify: `pkgs/evidence/report.py`, `tests/evidence/test_harness_report.py`, `docs/runbooks/evidence.md` **Interfaces:** - CLI: `report harness` gains `--split YYYY-MM-DD`: the baseline lines (SH1) print for the *before* window (`result_mtime[:10] < split`, further narrowed by `--since`) and a new block for the *after* window (`>= split`, narrowed by `--before`); without `--split` the block prints for the whole window. A malformed `--split` → exit 2, `report: --split : invalid date (YYYY-MM-DD)`. - `harness_report(store, before=None, since=None, split=None, min_n=5)`; the after-window block, after SH1's line 8: 9. `after: since before ; N task rows, G with a gate verdict, A approved` (A = gated rows with `gate.verdict == "approved"`). 10. One line per change, over the after-window rows whose change field is present (`touches_extra` not None for `touches`; `checks_verified` not None for `checks`; `probes_verified` not None for `probes`; every row for `unreported`): - `touches: n=; demotions (touches-violation); agreed (gate rejected); overruled (gate approved); ungated ; undisclosed extras rows` - `checks: n=; demotions checks-misreported , checks-unverifiable ; agreed ; overruled ; ungated ; verify-timeout ` - `probes: n=; demotions probe-mismatch , probe-missing ; agreed ; overruled ; ungated ; drift ` (`r` = rows whose `probes_verified` has a `drift` value) - `unreported: n=; gated ; approved ` A demotion is a row whose `error_class` is one of the change's arms; agreed = its gate `rejected`, overruled = its gate `approved`, ungated = no gate. `x` = rows with `touches_extra > touches_disclosed`. 11. `control false positives: of approved rows` (the overruled demotions of every change, summed, over the after window's approved gated rows). 12. One `verdict : …` line per change: over the change's gated demotions ordered by `result_mtime` (ties by `run_id`, `key`), the first five: `revert (overruled of 5)` when `o >= 2`, `keep (overruled of 5)` otherwise; fewer than five gated demotions → `insufficient (n=)`; and when the change's `n` (rows with the field) is at least 10 and its demotions are 0, the line ends `; zero demotions in tasks — keep only if the target tag fell to zero (tags unmeasured)`. 13. `success: first-gate approved before (

%) → after (%); output tokens per landing after against control median × 1.5 = <1.5 × the before window's approved median>: )>` — `yes` when the after median is at most the bound; `insufficient` when either approved set has fewer than `min_n` rows; `before` figures come from the before window, `after` from the after window; without `--split` the before figures print `-`. 14. `untargeted: never-ran-named-mutants, one-arm-per-enum, ignored-section-item — unmeasured in the store; proxy: mutants_outside_named summed over the after window's gates = over gates carrying the field`. - Consumers: the operator (Operator step 3); the orchestrator (a `revert` line → a `r` under rule A1). **Facts:** - SH1's `harness_report` and the fields SH3–SH5 declared (`touches_extra`, `touches_disclosed`, `checks_verified`, `probes_verified`, `derived`, the arms) — this task reads them through the join; Rule A1: this is SH5's one fix round; a second rejection re-plans.

**Fresh workspace, step 1 (before anything else):** the workspace is a fresh clone of main; bring SH5's commit in uncommitted with `git fetch -q /home/dalhaka/factory/ws/sh4/SH5 task/SH5 && git cherry-pick -n FETCH_HEAD` (the branch's one commit 31a69a3), then take main's generated files: `git checkout HEAD -- docs/OPERATIONS.md docs/MAP.md && git add docs/OPERATIONS.md docs/MAP.md` (`python3 pkgs/evidence/repomap.py --root . write` regenerates the map at Step 4). ONE commit at the end with this section's subject — SH5's subject is never reused.

**Contract — the review's items carried verbatim, each closed as stated:**

1. **MAJOR-1 (`tools/factory/seat/factory-brief:96-97`) — "The acceptance check `unit` is red: the brief rewrap splits the pinned phrase `no colon, no markdown`":** the section told the seat to add one sentence before "The first line is exactly the result line"; the seat re-flowed the whole paragraph so the phrase is no longer contiguous — base `line, one space, status=done|partial|failed — no colon, no markdown; any` became `… — no` / `colon, no markdown; any …`; three landed tests fail (`not ok 224` and `225` in `tests/unit/80-seat-driver.bats:2537,2552` on `[[ "$output" == *"no colon, no markdown"* ]]`, `not ok 503` in `94-seat-harness.bats:235`). Close: restore the paragraph's original line breaks byte for byte (lines 92–96 of the base `factory-brief`) and add the probe sentence as its OWN bullet line above the "End your final reply…" bullet, never re-flowing an existing line; `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.unit -L --no-link` green with the three tests `ok`. Mutant: re-flow the paragraph again → the three tests red (pasted).
2. **MAJOR-2 (`tools/factory/seat/factory-task:367`, `factory-lib.sh:772`) — "An `empty`/`nonempty` probe aborts the driver with `$3: unbound variable` and no `.result` is written at all":** `factory-task:367` calls `cmpv=$(factory_probe_compare "$pop" "$pdiver")` with two arguments while the function reads `local op=$1 bound=$2 value=$3` under `set -euo pipefail`; a scratch bats case with the plan's own `empty` shape aborted the driver (`line 772: $3: unbound variable`, no `.result`). Close: the driver always passes three arguments — `factory_probe_compare "$pop" "$pvalue" "$pdiver"` — and the function defaults every positional (`local op=${1-} bound=${2-} value=${3-}`); a new bats row drives an `empty` probe end to end through `factory-task` (the row-1 `checks-current` shape: `git status --porcelain docs/MAP.md :: empty :: the lint gate`) → the `.result` exists with `probes_verified: checks-current=pass` and `status=done`; a `nonempty` probe on `printf x` → `pass`; on `printf ''` → `fail`. Mutant: drop the third argument at the call site → the row red (no `.result`); pasted.
3. **MAJOR-3 (`tools/factory/seat/factory-task:348`) — "The driver's tab-split collapses the empty value column, so an `empty`/`nonempty` probe's command is lost":** `while IFS=$'\t' read -r pname pop pvalue pby pcmd` — tab is IFS whitespace, so a run of tabs collapses; `tasks.py probes` emits `dirt^Iempty^I^Ithe lint gate^Igit status --porcelain docs/MAP.md`, which the driver reads as `pvalue=[the lint gate] pby=[git status …] pcmd=[]` — the command empty, the provenance become the bound, and (with MAJOR-2 fixed) a probe that runs the empty string and passes unconditionally, the short-circuiting probe the spec's change 5 forbids. Close: split on a separator that is not IFS whitespace so empty fields survive — `line=${line//$'\t'/$'\x1f'}; IFS=$'\x1f' read -r pname pop pvalue pby pcmd <<<"$line"` (the unit separator never occurs in a probe line; `tasks.py check` refuses a tab in a command already); the end-to-end row of item 2 asserts `probes_verified: checks-current=pass` with the command actually run (the fake records its argv). Mutant: `IFS=$'\t'` put back → the row red (the command lost); pasted.
4. **MAJOR-4 (`tools/factory/seat/factory-lib.sh:777-785`; row 4) — "The section's named mutant for row 4b (`string compare for numbers`) survives":** the predicted red `ge 2 2.5 → pass` holds under a lexicographic compare too — a wrong fact of the section; every fixture in row 4 agrees with string order. Close: row 4 gains the discriminating pairs — `le 100 99` → pass, `lt 10 9` → pass, `ge 10 9` → fail, `gt 9 10` → pass, `le 8000 10000` → pass — each of which a string compare gets wrong. Mutant: the awk numeric block replaced by string comparisons → those rows red (pasted).
5. **MAJOR-5 (`tests/unit/94-seat-harness.bats:2262-2273`; row 14) — "The section's named mutant for row 14 (`put the line into the template`) survives and changes no test outcome anywhere":** the row asserts only `probe_pos < result_pos` and counts four known template lines, so a `FACTORY-PROBE` line placed directly above `FACTORY-RESULT` inside the template passes. Close: row 14 asserts the template block is the four lines `FACTORY-RESULT …` `FACTORY-CHECKS …` `FACTORY-COMMITS …` `FACTORY-NOTES …` CONTIGUOUS (the line immediately above `FACTORY-RESULT status=<…>` is the prose line ending `recorded as failed:`), and that `FACTORY-PROBE <name>=<value>` appears exactly once, inside the RULES bullet that names it, at least two lines above `FACTORY-RESULT`. Mutant: move the line into the template (directly above `FACTORY-RESULT`) → red; move it directly below `FACTORY-NOTES` → red; pasted.

Close: this commit's body pastes the real greens (`nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.unit -L --no-link` with the three tests' `ok` lines, `evidence-unit`, `lint`) and carries no Deviation line for an exempt file.

The review's other MINORs (the probe-name grammar refusal, the exit-status rule, the `ne`/`nonempty` true arms, the space folding, "the last per name", the 124 arm, the fail-and-missing arm, the `grep -v '<'` extraction) are recorded, not owed here.

**Files:**
- Create: `tools/factory/seat/factory-codex-usage.py`, `tests/unit/95-codex-arm.bats`
- Modify: `tools/factory/seat/factory-task`, `tools/factory/seat/factory-brief`, `tools/factory/seat/README.md`

**Interfaces:**

- **The arm select** (`factory-task`, after `export FACTORY_PLAN="$plan"` and before `kind_size=$(factory_task_kind_size "$plan" "$key")`): exactly `codex` selects the Codex arm; unset or empty is today's seat, byte for byte; any other value refuses with exit 2 and one stderr line `factory-task: FACTORY_SEAT=<value> is not a seat arm (unset it, or set it to codex)`, before `mkdir -p -- "$runs_dir"`, before the pid file, before `factory-ws` — nothing is written. `codex` with no `codex` on `PATH` refuses the same way (`factory-task: FACTORY_SEAT=codex but no codex on PATH`, exit 2, nothing written).


- **Model, effort, route, version and the brief's model under codex** (replacing the `route_line=$(factory_route …)` block for this arm only; the `else` branch is today's block, byte for byte). `factory_route` is not called; `OPENROUTER_MODEL` and `OPENROUTER_REASONING_EFFORT` are ignored, each with exactly one stderr line `factory-task: warning: OPENROUTER_MODEL is ignored under FACTORY_SEAT=codex` / `… OPENROUTER_REASONING_EFFORT …`; `route_label` is `explicit` with `--model`, else `codex/$kind/$size` (`factory_task_kind_size` prints `any any` for an untyped heading, so `codex/any/any` is possible and the fence maps it to `unknown` — CA3); `FACTORY_SEAT_VERSION` is the last whitespace token of `codex --version`'s first line when it matches `^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+([.-][0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$` (`codex-cli 0.153.4` → `0.153.4`), else unset with the warning `codex --version printed no version; the brief's trailer keeps its <version> placeholder`; `FACTORY_MODEL` (the brief's `<model>`) is the `--model` value, else the top-level `model` of `${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/config.toml`, else `unknown` (D5).

  and the existing `export FACTORY_MODEL=$model` becomes `export FACTORY_MODEL=$brief_model`.

- **`factory_codex_config_value <file> <key>`** (a function in `factory-task`, pure bash — the seat runs on the bare host PATH): prints the value of the first **top-level** line `<key> = "<value>"` (spaces optional around `=`; only a double-quoted value), reading lines only until the first line whose first non-blank character is `[` (a table header); prints nothing for an absent or unreadable file, an absent key, or a key that appears only inside a table; exit 0 always. `model_reasoning_effort` never matches the key `model` (the line must continue with `=` after the key and optional blanks).


- **No `DSH_HOME` under codex:** the `shared_dsh=…` / `factory_seed_dsh_home` block runs only for `seat_arm=dsh` (`if [ "$seat_arm" != codex ]; then … fi`); `dsh_home` stays unset and no `<KEY>.dsh-home` directory appears.

- **The launch** (a third arm, tested before `command -v seat-submit`): from the workspace clone (`cd -- "$ws"`, no `-C`, no `--skip-git-repo-check`), the brief on stdin, never `--ephemeral`, never `--json`; `-m "$model"` only with `--model`; the argv is exactly `exec -c features.plugins=false -c otel.metrics_exporter="none" --sandbox danger-full-access --color never [-m <model>] -`; stdout+stderr tee'd into `$log`; `exit_code` is `codex`'s (124 under `timeout`); `wall_s` as today.


- **The banner window and the three fields** (after the seat exits, before the result-line extraction; codex only). The banner is the block between the first two lines that are exactly `--------`; `model:`, `reasoning effort:` and `session id:` are read only inside it (D6). `model` = the banner's, else the config file's top-level `model`, else `unknown`; `effort` = the banner's `reasoning effort`, else the config's `model_reasoning_effort`, else `unknown` (the ingest maps anything outside `off|low|medium|high|xhigh` to `unknown` — its rule, not the driver's); `session_id` = the banner's `session id` when it is 36 hex-and-dash characters, else empty.


- **Usage under codex** (replacing the `sessions_dir=$dsh_home/sessions` block for this arm; `rm -f -- "$marker"` stays after both). With a session id: the one file `rollout-*-<id>.jsonl` under `$codex_home/sessions` (if several — impossible by construction — the last by name); a valid id whose file is missing logs `no rollout named by session id <id> under <dir>` and keeps `{}`. **Interfaces:**

**Contract — the review's items carried verbatim, each closed as stated:**

Close: in `setup`, compute `SAFE_PATH` — the current `PATH` with every directory that holds an executable `codex` removed (`IFS=:` walk; `[ -x "$d/codex" ] || keep`) — and `run_codex_task` (and every other invocation of the driver in this file) passes `PATH="$BIN:$SAFE_PATH"`. Row 2 then exits 2 with `FACTORY_SEAT=codex but no codex on PATH` on core exactly as in the build sandbox, `$REC` absent, no run dir. A new row 19 pins the helper: with the fake absent, `command -v codex` under the helper's PATH prints nothing (assert on a probe script the helper runs, or on `$output` of a row that `run`s `command -v codex` through the same PATH). Mutant: `PATH="$BIN:$PATH"` restored → row 2 red on core (the gate runs on core; in a codex-free sandbox both spellings pass — say so in the body).
2. **MAJOR-2 (`tests/unit/95-codex-arm.bats:381`) — "Row 8's `no seat: line` assertion cannot fail":** `! grep -q '^seat:' …` mid-test is inert under bats (`set -e` ignores a negated command that is not the test's last command); the section's named mutant — `[ "$seat_arm" = codex ] && [ -n "$session_id" ]` → `[ "$seat_arm" = codex ]` — writes `seat: codex ` (an empty id) and the row stays green. Close: every negated assertion in the file becomes a status-capturing one — `[ "$(grep -c '^seat:' "$f" || true)" -eq 0 ]` (or `run grep -c … ; [ "$output" = 0 ]`); audit the file: `grep -n '^[[:space:]]*!' tests/unit/95-codex-arm.bats` must print nothing after the change. Mutant: the empty-id line → row 8 red.
3. **MINOR-1 (`tools/factory/seat/factory-task:324`) — "the 36-hex-and-dash session-id rule has no fixture":** a row with `FAKE_SID=not-a-uuid` → no `seat:` line (the status-capturing form), and — the fake having written its rollout under `rollout-…-not-a-uuid.jsonl` — the usage still parsed through the newest-since-marker fallback (`"input": 68620`), the log line `no banner and no rollout` absent. Mutant: the regex loosened to `(.+)` → `seat: codex not-a-uuid` appears → red.
4. **MINOR-2 and MINOR-3 (`factory-task:793`, `:803`) — "the classifier copy's `.log`-free template and its removal are untested":** after the default row, `ls "$FACTORY_RUNS/r1"` holds no entry matching `.agent-*` and no `*.log` other than `K1.log` and `wave-*.log` (list the directory into `$output` and assert with `[[ … ]]` or `grep -c`, never a negated command). Mutants: the `rm -f` replaced by `:` → `.agent-K1.*` present → red; the template given a `.log` suffix → a second `*.log` → red.
5. **MINOR-6 (`factory-task:759`) — "the marker-branch refusal message has no assertion":** a row with `FAKE_NO_BANNER=1 FAKE_NO_ROLLOUT=1` → `usage: {}`, `error_class: boot-failure` (events 0, wall < 10), `$output` contains `no banner and no rollout newer than the launch marker`. Mutant: the message dropped → red.
6. **MINOR-4 and MINOR-5 — the section's own mutants that cannot discriminate:** row 6's second mutant (the window widened to EOF) is ill-posed — the banner's line precedes every decoy, so `head -n1` wins whatever the window; row 14's mutant (`$?` for `${PIPESTATUS[0]}`) is equivalent under `set -o pipefail`. Both are struck from the Tests table by this section (the plan's, recorded here); the rows' other mutants stand. No test is deleted.
7. **Pasted:** this commit's body pastes, under its command line, row 2's red on the cherry-picked tree (`not ok 2 … [ "$status" -eq 2 ]' failed`) and the new rows' reds (items 2–5), every mutant of items 1–5 shown red and reverted, and the greens (`bats tests/unit/95-codex-arm.bats tests/unit/80-seat-driver.bats tests/unit/94-seat-harness.bats`'s last line; `unit`'s and `lint`'s last lines).

Item 1's `SAFE_PATH` is the mechanism; check it before Step 2 with `PATH="$BIN:$SAFE_PATH" command -v codex` printing `$BIN/codex`, and with the fake removed printing nothing.

tasks.body:
**Files:**
- Create: `pkgs/helm-home/package.nix`, `pkgs/helm-home/portal.py`, `pkgs/helm-home/probe_result.py`, `pkgs/helm-home/probe.py`, `tests/helm-home/test_probe_result.py`, `tests/helm-home/test_portal.py`
- Modify: `flake.nix` (`helmHome = pkgs.callPackage ./pkgs/helm-home/package.nix { };` in the `let`; `packages.${system}.helm-home = helmHome;` and `packages.${system}.helm-home-probe` (below); `checks.helm-home-unit`, `checks.helm-home-package`; `pkgs/helm-home tests/helm-home` appended to both ruff lists of the `lint` check), `githooks/pre-commit` (the same two ruff lists), `docs/MAP.md` (regenerated — exempt)

**Interfaces:**
- `pkgs/helm-home/package.nix` — `{ lib, python3Packages, wrapGAppsHook4, gobject-introspection, gtk4, libadwaita, vte-gtk4, at-spi2-core }: python3Packages.buildPythonApplication { pname = "helm-home"; version = "0.1"; format = "other"; src = ./.; nativeBuildInputs = [ wrapGAppsHook4 gobject-introspection ]; buildInputs = [ gtk4 libadwaita vte-gtk4 at-spi2-core ]; propagatedBuildInputs = with python3Packages; [ pygobject3 pyatspi ]; dontWrapGApps = true; installPhase = ''install -Dm644 *.py -t $out/lib/helm-home; makeWrapper ${python3Packages.python.interpreter} $out/bin/helm-home-probe --add-flags $out/lib/helm-home/probe.py --prefix PYTHONPATH : $out/lib/helm-home:${../evidence} "''${gappsWrapperArgs[@]}"''; doInstallCheck = true; installCheckPhase = ''$out/bin/helm-home-probe --self-check | grep -F 'Gtk 4.' ''; meta.mainProgram = "helm-home-probe"; }`. Later tasks add entry points to this file (HH6 `helm-home-a11y`, HH7 `helm-home`); `../evidence` is `pkgs/evidence` (HH10's `refresh.py` imports `evidence`). `packages.helm-home-probe = pkgs.writeShellApplication { name = "helm-home-probe"; runtimeInputs = [ helmHome ]; text = ''exec helm-home-probe "$@"''; }` so `nix run .#helm-home-probe` works before HH7 flips `mainProgram`.
- `helm-home-probe [--out FILE] [--preferred-trigger TRIGGER] [--timeout SECONDS] [--self-check]` (`probe.py`; `gi` imported inside `main()` after argument parsing). `--self-check`: import `Gtk` 4, `Adw` 1, `Gio`; print `Gtk 4.<minor>.<micro> Adw 1.<minor>.<micro> portal org.freedesktop.portal.GlobalShortcuts`; exit 0 (no display needed). Otherwise: an `Adw.Application` with id `org.nixos_agent_env.HelmHome`, one window titled `Helm Home probe` (accessible name the same) showing the last event; on activate it calls `portal.request_raise(bus, app_id, on_bound, on_activated, preferred_trigger)` (default trigger `<Super>Return`); every event prints one stdout line: `probe: session <path>`, `probe: bind response=<n> bound=<true|false> trigger="<trigger_description or ->"`, `probe: activated <k> focus=<true|false>` (`focus` = the window's `is-active` property became true within 2 s of the signal); on window close or `--timeout` (default 600 s) it writes the record and prints `probe: verdict=<portal|fallback|unbound> bound=<b> activations=<k> focus_regained=<f>`. Exit 0 when a record was written; 2 on argument errors (argparse); 3 when the portal is unreachable (`Gio.DBusError` on `CreateSession`) with `probe: portal unreachable: <first line of the error>` on stderr and no record. `--out` default `$XDG_STATE_HOME/helm-home/probe.json` (`~/.local/state/helm-home/probe.json`), parent created 0700.
- `portal.py` (stdlib except an injected `bus` object with `call(interface, method, args) -> object path` and `subscribe(interface, signal, path, handler)`; `app.py` and `probe.py` pass a `Gio.DBusConnection` adapter): `request_tokens(counter) -> (handle_token, session_handle_token)` (`helm_home_<n>`); `shortcut_request(preferred_trigger) -> [("raise", {"description": "Raise Helm Home", "preferred_trigger": preferred_trigger})]` (with `preferred_trigger=None` the dict carries `description` only); `request_raise(bus, app_id, on_bound, on_activated, preferred_trigger=None)`: `CreateSession({handle_token, session_handle_token})` → on its `Response(0, {session_handle})` call `BindShortcuts(session_handle, shortcut_request(...), "", {handle_token})` → on its `Response(code, results)` call `on_bound(parse_bind_response(code, results))` → subscribe `Activated` on the session and call `on_activated(shortcut_id)` when `results`' `session_handle` matches. A `Response` with code ≠ 0 at either step calls `on_bound(BindResult(bound=False, trigger_description=None, response=code))` and subscribes to nothing.
- `probe_result.py` (pure): `BindResult(bound: bool, trigger_description: str | None, response: int)`; `parse_bind_response(response: int, results: dict) -> BindResult` — bound iff `response == 0` and `results.get("shortcuts")` holds an entry whose id is `raise` (the entry shape is `(id, {description, trigger_description})`; a list of two-item lists is accepted too — GLib's JSON-ish variants unpack to lists); `verdict(bound, activations, focus_regained) -> str`: `unbound` when not bound; `portal` when bound and `activations >= 1` and `focus_regained == activations`; `fallback` otherwise; `record(bound_result, activations, focus_regained, now) -> dict` with exactly the keys `schema` (1), `ts` (RFC3339 `Z`), `bind_response`, `bound`, `trigger_description`, `activations`, `focus_regained`, `verdict`.
- `checks.helm-home-unit` = `pkgs.runCommand "helm-home-unit" { nativeBuildInputs = [ helmPython pkgs.git ]; } ''mkdir -p pkgs tests; cp -r ${self}/pkgs/helm-home pkgs/helm-home; cp -r ${self}/pkgs/evidence pkgs/evidence; cp -r ${self}/tests/helm-home tests/helm-home; export HOME=$TMPDIR GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=$TMPDIR/.gitconfig; pytest tests/helm-home -q; touch $out''` (git for HH10's accept tests; `helmPython` is the existing `python3.withPackages (ps: [ ps.pytest ])`). Tests load modules by path like `tests/helm/test_serve.py` does (`importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`).
- `checks.helm-home-package = helmHome;` — the package's own `installCheckPhase` is the check.

**Facts (planning time):** the pin, the portal file and the interface (Assumptions 1–2); `nix eval --offline .#checks.x86_64-linux.helm-home-unit` → `error: flake 'git+file:///home/dalhaka/nixos-agent-env' does not provide attribute 'packages.x86_64-linux.checks.x86_64-linux.helm-home-unit', 'legacyPackages.x86_64-linux.checks.x86_64-linux.helm-home-unit' or 'checks.x86_64-linux.helm-home-unit'`; `ls pkgs | grep -c helm-home` → `0`; the ruff lists (Assumption 7); `helm-unit`'s shape (Assumption 4). The spec's D-H3 names "xdg-desktop-portal-gnome 48 on the host pin"; the pin is 50.0 (D11).

- [ ] **Step 1: the failing check.** Write `tests/helm-home/test_probe_result.py` and `tests/helm-home/test_portal.py` (Tests below), add the two ruff list entries, wire `helm-home-unit` and `helm-home-package` in `flake.nix` with `package.nix` present, `git add` everything. Red: `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.helm-home-unit -L --no-link` → pytest prints `ERROR tests/helm-home/test_probe_result.py` with `FileNotFoundError: … pkgs/helm-home/probe_result.py` (the loader's path) and `error: builder for '/nix/store/…-helm-home-unit.drv' failed with exit code 1`. Paste both lines.
- [ ] **Step 2: the pure modules.** `probe_result.py`, `portal.py`. Green: the same command → `… passed` and the derivation builds.
- [ ] **Step 3: the probe and the package.** `probe.py`, the `installCheckPhase`. Green: `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.helm-home-package -L --no-link` (the log shows `Gtk 4.22.4 Adw 1.9.3 portal org.freedesktop.portal.GlobalShortcuts`); `nix build .#packages.x86_64-linux.helm-home-probe --no-link --print-out-paths`. The seat cannot run the window (no display); the operator's step 2 is the measurement.
- [ ] **Step 4: lint and MAP.** `python3 pkgs/evidence/repomap.py --root . write`; `nix develop -c githooks/pre-commit`; `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.lint -L --no-link`. One commit.

**Tests** (`tests/helm-home/test_probe_result.py`, `test_portal.py`; one assertion per row, the mutant beside it):

| # | assertion | discriminating fixture row | one-line mutant that turns it red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `parse_bind_response(0, {"shortcuts": [("raise", {"description": "Raise Helm Home", "trigger_description": "Super+Return"})]})` → `bound=True`, `trigger_description="Super+Return"` | the id `raise` with a trigger text | `bound = response == 0` (ignore the list): row 2 stays bound → red |
| 2 | `parse_bind_response(0, {"shortcuts": []})` → `bound=False` | the empty subset the interface allows | same mutant as row 1 |
| 3 | `parse_bind_response(1, {"shortcuts": [("raise", {...})]})` → `bound=False`, `response=1` | cancelled with a non-empty list | drop the `response == 0` gate → red |
| 4 | `parse_bind_response(0, {"shortcuts": [("other", {...})]})` → `bound=False` | another id only | `any(True for _ in shortcuts)` (any entry counts) → red |
| 5 | `parse_bind_response(0, {"shortcuts": [["raise", {"trigger_description": "x"}]]})` → bound (list-shaped entries) | the list-of-lists shape | `isinstance(entry, tuple)` only → red |
| 6 | `verdict(True, 2, 2)` → `portal`; `verdict(True, 2, 1)` → `fallback`; `verdict(True, 0, 0)` → `fallback`; `verdict(False, 3, 3)` → `unbound` | the four arms, each its own assertion line | `focus_regained >= 1` instead of `== activations` → the (2, 1) row reads portal → red; drop the bound gate → the (False, 3, 3) row reads portal → red; `activations >= 0` → the (0, 0) row reads portal → red |

| 8 | `shortcut_request("<Super>Return")` == `[("raise", {"description": "Raise Helm Home", "preferred_trigger": "<Super>Return"})]`; `shortcut_request(None)` carries no `preferred_trigger` key | both arms | always emit `preferred_trigger` (None) → red |

**Files:**
- Create: `nixosModules/helmHome.nix`
- Modify: `flake.nix` (`nixosModules.helmHome`; the `coreModules`/`mkCore` refactor of `nixosConfigurations.core`; the fixture systems `helmHomeSystem`, `helmHomeBadEnableSystem`, `helmHomeBadPathSystem`, `helmHomeBadProfileSystem`, `helmHomeBadSeatsSystem`, `helmHomeBadDuplicateSystem`; checks `helm-home-eval`, `helm-home-assertion-negative-enable`, `-path`, `-profile`, `-seats`, `-duplicate`, `helm-home-reversible`), `docs/MAP.md` (regenerated — exempt)

**Interfaces:**
1. **Options** (`nixosModules/helmHome.nix`, header `{ config, lib, ... }:`): `services.helm.home.enable` (`mkEnableOption "Helm Home: the home screen (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-04-helm-home-design.md)"`); `services.helm.home.package` (`types.package`, no default: the host passes the flake's `helm-home`, a fixture passes a stub — HH9 wires the host); `services.helm.home.flakes` (`listOf (submodule ({ config, ... }: { options = { path (str, required, "Absolute path of the flake checkout"); declaration (str, default "${config.path}#helm", defaultText "\"<path>#helm\""); profile (nullOr str, default null); seats (listOf (enum [ "claude" "deepseek" ]), default [ ]); }; }))`, default `[ ]`).
2. **Assertions** (all under `mkIf cfg.enable`, one per D-H4 rule, exact messages): (E) `helm.enable && helm.control.enable` → `services.helm.home requires services.helm.enable and services.helm.control.enable (the helm-switch@ unit and its polkit rule)`; (P) every `path` `hasPrefix "/"` → `services.helm.home.flakes: every path must be absolute; offenders: <space-joined>`; (R) every `profile` null or `elem` `helm.control.profiles` → `services.helm.home.flakes: profile must be null or one of <profiles>; offenders: <space-joined>`; (D) `length (unique paths) == length paths` → `services.helm.home.flakes: a path is declared twice`; (S) seats — the enum type refuses at eval (a type error, not an assertion).
3. **Rendering** (under `mkIf cfg.enable`, nothing else): `environment.etc."helm/home.json" = { text = builtins.toJSON { schema = 1; flakes = map (f: { inherit (f) path declaration profile seats; }) cfg.flakes; }; mode = "0644"; }` (the consumer is HH5's `load_home`); `environment.etc."xdg/autostart/helm-home.desktop" = { text = ''[Desktop Entry]\nType=Application\nName=Helm Home\nExec=${cfg.package}/bin/helm-home\nOnlyShowIn=GNOME;\nX-GNOME-Autostart-Phase=Application\n''; mode = "0644"; }`; `environment.systemPackages = [ cfg.package ]`. No GNOME setting, no polkit change (HH2's), no user unit (D7).
4. **`mkCore`** (`flake.nix`): `coreSpecialArgs = { claude-code-pkg = …; … inherit claude-desktop; }` and `coreModules = [ ./hosts/core self.nixosModules.basketStore … gaming.nixosModules.default (_: { system.configurationRevision = …; }) ]` — today's literal lists lifted into the `let`; `mkCore = modules: nixpkgs-host.lib.nixosSystem { system = "x86_64-linux"; specialArgs = coreSpecialArgs; inherit modules; };`; `nixosConfigurations.core = mkCore (coreModules ++ [ self.nixosModules.helmHome ]);` (imported, disabled — `hosts/core` sets nothing under `services.helm.home` until HH9).
5. **Checks.** `helm-home-eval` (fixture `helmHomeSystem` = `helmControlSystem`'s node plus `self.nixosModules.helmHome`, `services.helm.home = { enable = true; package = pkgs.writeShellScriptBin "helm-home" ":"; flakes = [ { path = "/var/lib/fake-repo"; profile = "alt"; seats = [ "deepseek" ]; } { path = "/var/lib/other"; } ]; }`): Nix assertions `c.environment.etc."helm/home.json".mode == "0644"`, `hasInfix "/bin/helm-home" c.environment.etc."xdg/autostart/helm-home.desktop".text`, `any (p: (p.name or "") == "helm-home") c.environment.systemPackages`, `c.services.helm.control.workspaces == { }`, then a `runCommand` with `jq` over the rendered text (`passAsFile`): `.schema == 1`, `.flakes|length == 2`, `.flakes[0].declaration == "/var/lib/fake-repo#helm"`, `.flakes[0].profile == "alt"`, `.flakes[0].seats == ["deepseek"]`, `.flakes[1].declaration == "/var/lib/other#helm"`, `.flakes[1].profile == null`, `.flakes[1].seats == []`, and `builtins.seq c.system.build.toplevel.drvPath`. Each negative fixture is `helmHomeSystem` with one change: `-enable` (`services.helm.control.enable = lib.mkForce false`), `-path` (`path = "relative/x"`), `-profile` (`profile = "nope"`), `-seats` (`seats = [ "claude" "gpt" ]`), `-duplicate` (two entries with `path = "/var/lib/fake-repo"`); each check is `builtins.tryEval <bad>.config.system.build.toplevel.drvPath` → must fail, and for the four assertion rules the failing message set (`map (a: a.message) (filter (a: !a.assertion) c.assertions)`) must contain the rule's exact message prefix (`throw "<check>: failed but did not name the rule (got: …)"` otherwise); `-seats` is the type error, `tryEval` alone. `helm-home-reversible`: `let withHome = (mkCore (coreModules ++ [ self.nixosModules.helmHome { services.helm.home.enable = nixpkgs.lib.mkForce false; } ])).config.system.build.toplevel.drvPath; without = (mkCore coreModules).config.system.build.toplevel.drvPath; in if withHome == without then pkgs.runCommand "helm-home-reversible-ok" { } "touch $out" else throw "helm-home-reversible: the toplevel with services.helm.home.enable = false (${withHome}) differs from the host without the module (${without})"`.

**Facts (planning time):** Assumption 7 (the core definition, the fixture and negative shapes, `helmControlSystem`); `grep -c 'services.helm.home' nixosModules/helm.nix hosts/core/*.nix flake.nix` → `0` for each; `nix eval --offline .#checks.x86_64-linux.helm-home-eval` → `error: flake '…' does not provide attribute … 'checks.x86_64-linux.helm-home-eval'`; the option style of `services.helm.control.workspaces` (a `submodule` with `path`, absolute-path assertion `services.helm.control: every workspace path must be absolute`).

- [ ] **Step 1: red.** Wire the six fixtures and seven checks and the `mkCore` refactor with `self.nixosModules.helmHome = import ./nixosModules/helmHome.nix` pointing at an EMPTY module file (`_: { }`), `git add`. Red: `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.helm-home-eval -L --no-link` → `error: The option 'services.helm.home.enable' does not exist. Definition values: - In '/nix/store/…-source/flake.nix': true`; `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.helm-home-assertion-negative-path -L --no-link` → the same error inside `tryEval` is not caught (an undefined option is an evaluation error), so the check itself errors — paste it; `helm-home-reversible` is green already (an empty module adds nothing) — that is the point: paste `helm-home-reversible-ok` and keep it green through every step; `host-core` green (the refactor changes no module).
- [ ] **Step 2: the module.** Green: the seven checks; `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.host-core -L --no-link`; `nix eval --raw .#nixosConfigurations.core.config.system.build.toplevel.drvPath` prints one path (the refactor still evaluates).
- [ ] **Step 3: MAP, lint, one commit.** `python3 pkgs/evidence/repomap.py --root . write` (seven new names); `nix develop -c githooks/pre-commit`.

**Tests** (each row a check assertion or a fixture; the mutant beside it):

| # | assertion | discriminating row | mutant |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `-enable`: home enabled with `control.enable = false` fails naming `services.helm.home requires services.helm.enable and services.helm.control.enable` | control off, helm on | drop assertion (E) → the fixture builds → `DID NOT FAIL` red |
| 2 | `-path`: `relative/x` fails naming `every path must be absolute; offenders: relative/x` | one relative path beside one absolute | drop (P) → red; `hasInfix "/"` instead of `hasPrefix` → `relative/x` passes → red |
| 3 | `-profile`: `nope` fails naming `profile must be null or one of base alt; offenders: nope` | a name outside `[ base alt ]` | drop (R) → red; check only non-null-ness → red |
| 4 | `-seats`: `[ "claude" "gpt" ]` fails to evaluate | one valid seat beside one invalid | `listOf types.str` → the fixture builds → red |
| 5 | `-duplicate`: two entries with the same path fail naming `a path is declared twice` | two identical paths with different profiles | drop (D) → red |
| 6 | `helm-home-eval` jq rows: the default `declaration` is `<path>#helm` for both entries | the entry with no explicit declaration | default `"#helm"` → red; default from a literal path → the second entry red |
| 7 | `helm-home-eval`: `profile` null and `seats` `[]` render as JSON `null` and `[]` (never omitted) | the second entry | `filterAttrs (n: v: v != null)` before `toJSON` → `.flakes[1].profile == null` red |
| 8 | `helm-home-eval`: `mode == "0644"`; the autostart text carries `/bin/helm-home` and `OnlyShowIn=GNOME;`; the package is a system package | — | `mode = "0600"` → red; `Exec=helm-home` (bare) → red |
| 9 | `helm-home-eval`: `control.workspaces == { }` on the fixture (the parked option untouched by this module) | — | the module setting `control.workspaces` → red |
| 10 | `helm-home-reversible`: the two drvPaths are equal | core itself | `environment.etc."helm/home.json"` (a constant text) moved outside `mkIf cfg.enable` → the paths differ → red naming both |
| 11 | `host-core` still evaluates and every existing assertion holds after the `mkCore` refactor (`hc.workspaces == { }`, the polkit enumeration, …) | core | drop a module from `coreModules` → `host-core` red |

**probes:**
- checks-wired: `grep -c '^        helm-home-' flake.nix` :: ge 7 :: seven check names at the repomap indent

equal to `facts.head` → `current`; else `git -C path merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD` rc 0 → `changed`, any other rc → `unknown`. - `declaration_check(entry, run) -> str | None`: `run(["nix", "eval", "--offline", "--raw", f"{entry.path}#checks.x86_64-linux.helm-declaration.drvPath"])`; `write-card` iff `decl_or_face` is a `Face` of kind `no-declaration`; `refresh` iff a `Declaration`. When `check_message` is not `None`, `switch` and `run` verbs carry `disabled_reason = check_message`. - `card(entry, decl_or_face, facts_or_face, marker) -> Card(title, summary, stamp, marker, blocks)`: with a `Declaration`, `blocks` = `[(kind, lines)]` in `decl.card.blocks` order, `why`/`state`/`notes` from the declaration, `do` from `verbs`, `cost`/`lastRun`/`terminal` as `("cost", ["no data yet"])` placeholders, an unknown block kind as `(kind, ["unknown block"])`; with a `Face`, `title` = the path's basename, `blocks` = `[("facts", [head/short/date/subject/branch/dirty lines or the face's reason])]`; `stamp` = `f"updated {decl.updated}"` or `"no card yet"`; `marker` = the `changed_since` word. - `strip(status_path, now) -> Strip(state, age_s, tiles, generation, active_profile)`: missing/unparsable → `state="missing"`, `tiles=[]`; `generated_at` older than `2 * interval_s` seconds → `state="stale"`, `age_s` the difference; else `state="live"`; `tiles = [(name, status, since)]` for every tile in the document, in document order. - `apply_sheet(entry, facts, strip, run, root="/nix/var/nix/profiles/system") -> Sheet(ok, reason, diff, last_check, rollback)`: refusals in this order, the first wins: `entry.profile is None` → `("not offered")`; `facts` is a `Face` → its reason; `facts.dirty` → `dirty tree`; a `flake-check` tile with status `fail` → `red checks: flake-check fail since `; the target binary missing (`/bin/switch-to-configuration` for `base`, `/specialisation/

/bin/switch-to-configuration` otherwise) → `profile

is not built into the registered generation`; else `ok` with `diff` = the stdout of `run(["nix", "store", "diff-closures", "/run/current-system", ])` truncated to 4,096 bytes, `last_check` = `flake-check since ` (or `no status`), `rollback` = `Switch to ` (the same prompt, spec §5). **Facts (planning time):** the document shape and tile names (Assumption 9); the switch script's root and binary paths (Assumption 16); the repos.toml names equal their basenames (Assumption 11); `tests/helm/test_serve.py` loads modules by path (`importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`, Assumption 4) — the same idiom here; HH1's `helm-home-unit` runs `pytest tests/helm-home -q` with git available. - [ ] **Step 1: red.** Write the three fixtures and `tests/helm-home/test_model.py`. **Files:**
- Create: `pkgs/helm-home/a11y.py`, `tests/helm-home/test_a11y_cli.py`, `tests/integration/helm-home-session-vm.nix`
- Modify: `pkgs/helm-home/probe.py` (the `--spike` mode), `pkgs/helm-home/package.nix` (the `helm-home-a11y` entry point), `flake.nix` (`checks.helm-home-session-vm`), `docs/MAP.md` (regenerated — exempt)

**Interfaces:**
1. `helm-home-probe --spike`: no portal; one `Gtk.ApplicationWindow` titled `Helm Home spike` (accessible name the same) with two `Gtk.Button`s labelled `Spike press` (sensitive; pressing it writes `$XDG_STATE_HOME/helm-home/spike-pressed`, parent created, and prints `probe: spike pressed`) and `Spike off` (`set_sensitive(False)`); exit 0 on close.
2. `helm-home-a11y [--timeout S] <verb> --app APP --role ROLE --name NAME` (`a11y.py`; `pyatspi` imported inside `main()`): verbs `find` (prints `found <app>/<role>/<name>` exit 0, or `not-found` exit 1 after `--timeout`, default 30 s, polling every 0.5 s), `press` (`find`, then `doAction(0)` on the node's `Action` interface; prints `pressed`; exit 1 when not found, 2 when the node has no action), `sensitive` (prints `sensitive` or `insensitive` — `pyatspi.STATE_SENSITIVE` in `getState().getStates()`; exit 1 when not found), `text` (prints the node's `name` then its `Text` interface content when present; exit 1 when not found). Matching is exact on the app's name and the node's name, the role compared to `node.getRoleName()` (strings like `frame`, `push button`, `list item`, `label`, `dialog`); the search is a breadth-first walk from `pyatspi.Registry.getDesktop(0)` over the named app only. Pure, tested without a bus: `parse_args(argv) -> Command`, `matches(node_name, node_role, want_name, want_role) -> bool`, `verdict_line(verb, found, has_action, sensitive) -> (stdout, exit_code)`.
3. `package.nix`: a second wrapper `helm-home-a11y` (`makeWrapper … --add-flags $out/lib/helm-home/a11y.py …`), and `installCheckPhase` also runs `$out/bin/helm-home-a11y --help | grep -F 'find'`.
4. **The VM** (`tests/integration/helm-home-session-vm.nix`, `{ pkgs, helmHome }`, `pkgs.testers.runNixOSTest`): the node imports `"${pkgs.path}/nixos/tests/common/user-account.nix"` (alice, uid 1000); GDM + autologin alice + GNOME exactly as nixpkgs' `gnome.nix`, including the `org.gnome.Shell@` `--unsafe-mode` override (needed for the `Main.layoutManager._startingUp` poll); `virtualisation.memorySize = 3072; virtualisation.cores = 2;`; `environment.systemPackages = [ helmHome ]`. Script: `wait_for_unit("display-manager.service")`, `wait_for_file("/run/user/1000/wayland-0")`, `wait_for_unit("default.target", "alice")`, the `startingUp` poll, `send_key("esc")`; then `run "systemd-run --user --collect --unit helm-home-spike helm-home-probe --spike"` (`run = command: "su - alice -c 'DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/1000/bus ${command}'"`); then `wait_until_succeeds(run "helm-home-a11y --timeout 5 find --app helm-home-probe --role frame --name 'Helm Home spike'")` — the app name AT-SPI reports is the process's application name (`Gio.Application` sets it from `GLib.set_prgname` → `helm-home-probe`; the spike sets `GLib.set_prgname("helm-home-probe")` explicitly), `succeed(run "helm-home-a11y sensitive --app helm-home-probe --role 'push button' --name 'Spike off'")` → output `insensitive`, `… --name 'Spike press'` → `sensitive`, `succeed(run "helm-home-a11y press --app helm-home-probe --role 'push button' --name 'Spike press'")` → `pressed`, `wait_for_file("/home/alice/.local/state/helm-home/spike-pressed")`, `machine.screenshot("spike")`. Wired: `helm-home-session-vm = import ./tests/integration/helm-home-session-vm.nix { inherit pkgs helmHome; };`.

**Facts (planning time):** Assumptions 1 (pyatspi 2.58.1, at-spi2-core 2.60.4, gnome-shell 50.4), 12 (the nixpkgs GNOME test's incantations, the driver's helpers), 13 (the AT-SPI role names — the assumption this task tests); no VM test in this repo boots a graphical session; `virtualisation.memorySize` is a plain option (`nixos/modules/virtualisation/qemu-vm.nix`). GTK 4 does not need `GTK_A11Y=atspi` (its default on Linux); if the first run finds nothing, the variable is the one knob to record in the commit body (and the test sets it explicitly for the spike so the result is reproducible).

- [ ] **Step 1: red (pure).** `tests/helm-home/test_a11y_cli.py`; red: `nix develop -c pytest tests/helm-home -q` → `ERROR tests/helm-home/test_a11y_cli.py - FileNotFoundError: … pkgs/helm-home/a11y.py`. Paste it. Then `a11y.py` → green.
- [ ] **Step 2: red (the check).** Wire the VM check with the test script above, `git add`; red: `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.helm-home-session-vm -L --no-link` → the VM boots and `helm-home-a11y … find` prints `not-found` until `probe.py` has the `--spike` mode (the unit `helm-home-spike` fails: `error: unrecognized arguments: --spike`) → `wait_until_succeeds` times out → `error: builder for '…-vm-test-run-helm-home-session.drv' failed`. Paste the log's `not-found` line. (Long; ≈ 5–8 min a run on core.)
- [ ] **Step 3: green.** `--spike` in `probe.py`, the package wrapper; `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.helm-home-session-vm -L --no-link` green; paste the log lines `found helm-home-probe/frame/Helm Home spike`, `insensitive`, `sensitive`, `pressed`. Record in the commit body whether `GTK_A11Y` had to be set.
- [ ] **Step 4: MAP, lint, one commit.**

**Tests:**

| # | assertion | discriminating row | mutant |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `parse_args(["find","--app","a","--role","frame","--name","X"])` → `Command("find","a","frame","X", timeout=30)`; `--timeout 5` parsed as float | both | default timeout 0 → the first row red |
| 2 | `matches("Helm Home spike", "frame", "Helm Home spike", "frame")` True; a case-different name False; a prefix False; role `push button` vs `frame` False | four rows | `startswith` → the prefix row red; lower-casing → the case row red |
| 3 | `verdict_line("sensitive", found=True, has_action=False, sensitive=False)` → `("insensitive", 0)`; `found=False` → `("not-found", 1)`; `press` with `has_action=False` → exit 2 | three rows | exit 0 on not-found → red |
| 4 | VM: `find … 'Helm Home spike'` succeeds within the timeout | the spike window | the spike's title changed to `x` → `not-found` → red |
| 5 | VM: `sensitive … 'Spike off'` prints `insensitive`, `… 'Spike press'` prints `sensitive` | both buttons | drop `set_sensitive(False)` → red; read `STATE_ENABLED` and print `insensitive` for both → the second row red |
| 6 | VM: `press` prints `pressed` and the marker file appears | the sensitive button | `doAction(1)` → `not-found`/no file → red |
| 7 | package: `helm-home-a11y --help` names `find` (the install check) | the wrapper | drop the wrapper → red |

Adw 1. Vte 3.91` and exits 0 without a display. Otherwise an `Adw.Application` (id `org.nixos_agent_env.HelmHome`, `GLib.set_prgname("helm-home")`) with one `Adw.ApplicationWindow` titled `Helm Home` (accessible name the same), `fullscreen()` unless `--no-fullscreen`, no header bar (an `Adw.ToolbarView` with the strip as its top bar). 2. **Widgets and their accessible names** (the VM drives by these; every name is a rule, not a decoration): the list — a `Gtk.ListBox` named `flakes`, one `Gtk.ListBoxRow` per entry named the card title (the declaration's `name`, else the path's basename), a dot label named `attention` when `verbs`' entry has a `Face`, `facts.dirty`, or marker `changed`; the card — a vertical `Gtk.Box` named `card`, a title label, the summary, the stamp label (`updated ` | `no card yet`) and the marker label named `changed-since` (`changed` | `current` | `unknown`), then one child per `Card.blocks` entry in order; the `do` block's buttons named exactly the verb labels from `model.verbs` (`Switch to

`, `Run:

`, with CSS class `grey` and the text `no status` / `stale s` when the strip is missing/stale, each label clickable (`Gtk.GestureClick`) to open a detail tile with the tile's `summary`; the drawer — an `Adw.TabView` named `drawer` with an `Adw.TabBar`, tiles are `Vte.Terminal`s or `Gtk.TextView`s, a tile's `pop out` (the tab's context menu) moves the page to a new `Adw.Window` via `transfer_page`. 3. **Verbs → processes** (`actions.py`, pure): `run_argv(entry, command) -> ["nix", "run", "--offline", f"{entry.path}#{tok}", "--", *rest]` where `tok` is the first whitespace token and `rest` the remaining `shlex.split` tokens (an empty command → `ValueError`); `seat_argv(seat) -> ["claude"] | ["dsh-openrouter"]` (`ValueError` otherwise), always run with `cwd=entry.path`; `switch_argv(profile) -> ["systemctl", "start", f"helm-switch@{profile}.service"]`; `journal_argv(profile) -> ["journalctl", "-fu", f"helm-switch@{profile}.service", "-n", "20", "--no-pager"]`; `tile_title(verb) -> str`. A `Run` or `Work here` press spawns a `Vte.Terminal` tile (`spawn_async` with the argv, `cwd`, the session's environment); the terminal's exit prints `[exited ]` into the tile. 4. **Switch flow.** Press → `model.apply_sheet` → an `Adw.AlertDialog` named `Switch to

` with the body: the diff (a monospace `Gtk.TextView`), `last check: `, `rollback: `; responses `cancel` and `apply` (the `apply` button named `Apply`). `Apply` → `Gio.Subprocess.new(switch_argv(p), STDOUT_PIPE | STDERR_PIPE)` — polkit's session agent asks for the password on its own; a progress tile (`journal_argv`) opens in the drawer; on exit the card shows a banner label named `switch-result`: exit 0 → `Now running:

. Rollback: Switch to .` and the strip is re-read; exit ≠ 0 → `Switch to

failed (exit ); see the journal tile. Rollback: Switch to .` with the tile kept open; a dismissed dialog (`Interactive authentication required` on stderr) is the failure face with that line. 5. **The raise key.** On `activate`, `portal.request_raise(GioBusAdapter(session_bus), app_id, on_bound, on_activated, preferred_trigger="Return")` (HH1's module; the adapter maps `call` to `Gio.DBusConnection.call_sync` on `org.freedesktop.portal.Desktop` / `/org/freedesktop/portal/desktop` and `subscribe` to `signal_subscribe`); `on_activated` → `window.present()`; `on_bound` with `bound=False` or a D-Bus error → one stderr line `helm-home: raise key: ` and the app continues (the fallback is the operator's decision from HH1's verdict, §Not in this plan). 6. **Refresh timers:** the strip re-reads `--status` every 30 s (`GLib.timeout_add_seconds`); the list and the selected card re-read on window focus-in and every 300 s; a failure of any read is a face on the card, never an exception out of a callback (every callback body is wrapped: an exception becomes one stderr line `helm-home: : : `). 7. **Failure faces** (spec §5): missing path → the row's title struck through (Pango `strikethrough`) and the reason in the card; **Files:**
- Create: `pkgs/helm-home/refresh.py`, `tests/helm-home/test_refresh.py`, `tests/helm-home/fixtures/lane-output.json`, `tests/helm-home/fixtures/helm-canonical.nix`
- Modify: `pkgs/helm-home/app.py` (the `refresh` and `write this card` buttons: spinner → diff → accept/reject; the job id on the button after a failure)

**Interfaces** (`refresh.py`; stdlib plus `evidence` from `pkgs/evidence`; every process through the injected `run`; `now` and `store` injected):
1. `payload(entry, decl_text, run, store, name) -> Payload(sections: dict, bytes: int)` with exactly three sections, each a string capped at 4,000 bytes (a cut section ends with `\n[cut]`): `git` = `git -C <path> log -n 20 --format=%h%x09%cs%x09%s` (stdout; rc ≠ 0 → `no git log`); `checks` = the sorted keys of `.checks."x86_64-linux"` from `nix flake show --offline --json <path>` (rc ≠ 0 → `no checks readable`), at most 30 names; `ledger` = the newest 10 rows of `evidence.read(store, "derived/tasks")` whose `repo == name` (name = the path's basename, Assumption 11), rendered `ts key status model wall_s` per line, only those five fields, `no ledger rows` when none; `decl_text` = the current `helm.nix` text or `none — write the first declaration`. `messages(payload) -> list[{role, content}]`: one `system` message (the schema: the ten fields, the block kinds, the seats, the caps `summary ≤ 120 chars, why ≤ 300, state ≤ 300, notes ≤ 500`; "reply with the complete helm.nix as one ```nix fenced block and nothing else"; "never change name, created, owner"), one `user` message with the four parts under fixed headings. The messages JSON is what `lane-submit` reads on stdin.
2. `submit(messages, run, model="deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash") -> str`: `run(["lane-submit", "openrouter", "--kind", "chat", "--class", "permitted", "--model", model], stdin=json)`; the id is the last non-empty stdout line and must match `^[0-9a-f]{12}$`, else `RefreshError("submit", <first stderr line or the offending line>)`; `wait(job_id, run, timeout=300) -> str`: `run(["lane-wait", "openrouter", job_id, "--timeout", str(timeout)])`; rc ≠ 0 or a result with an `error` key → `RefreshError("job-failed", job_id=job_id, detail=<error or first stderr line>)`; returns `result["output"]`.
3. `proposal(output, current: dict | None, head: str, today: str) -> Proposal(new_text, diff)`: exactly one ```nix fence (zero or more than one → `RefreshError("no-proposal")`); the fenced text must evaluate: `run(["nix", "eval", "--offline", "--json", "--expr", f"import {tmpfile}"])` rc 0 (else `RefreshError("bad-proposal", first stderr line)`) — the JSON object then passes the structural rules in Python (`check_shape(obj) -> list[str]`: the same F1–F6, O1, O3-shape, O4, C1–C3 strings as HH4's checker; O2 and the program lookup are the flake's own check, not the app's); `name`, `created`, `owner` must equal the current declaration's (or, for a first card, `name` must equal the basename) → else `RefreshError("bad-proposal", "name/created/owner changed")`; then `obj["updated"] = today`, `obj["writtenAgainst"] = head` regardless of the reply (D8); `new_text = to_nix(obj)`; `diff = "".join(difflib.unified_diff(current_text_lines, new_lines, "helm.nix", "helm.nix (proposed)"))`.
4. `to_nix(obj) -> str`: a canonical renderer — attributes sorted, two-space indent, one list element per line, strings escaped (`\` → `\\`, `"` → `\"`, `${` → `\${`, newline → `\n`), `null` for `None`, lists `[ ]` when empty; the fixture `helm-canonical.nix` is the golden text for this repo's declaration dict.
5. `accept(entry, proposal, head, job_id, model, run) -> str`: precondition `git -C <path> rev-parse HEAD` == `head` (the tree moved → `RefreshError("stale", …)`); write `<path>/helm.nix`; `git -C <path> add helm.nix`; `git -C <path> commit -q -m "helm: card refreshed <today>" -m "Generated-By: helm-home refresh / <model> (lane job <job_id>)"`; returns the new HEAD. `reject(...)` writes nothing. `export_line(entry, run) -> str | None`: `None` when `nix eval --offline --json <path>#helm` succeeds, else the string `helm = import ./helm.nix;` for the card to show (D10).
6. **In `app.py`**: `refresh` / `write this card` press → the button shows a spinner and is insensitive; a worker thread runs `payload → submit → wait → proposal`; the result lands on the main loop (`GLib.idle_add`): a side-by-side view (`Gtk.Paned`: current text | proposed text) with the diff below and two buttons named `accept` and `reject`; `accept` → `accept()` then the card re-reads (`stamp` = today, marker `current`) and, for a first card, a label named `export-line` with the line to add; `reject` → nothing written; a `RefreshError` → the card unchanged, the button's label `refresh failed · job <id>` (or `refresh failed · <kind>` before a job id exists), the detail in a tooltip and one stderr line.

**Facts (planning time):** Assumption 10 (the lane CLI, the id shape, the result file, the model, the group); Assumption 14 (`evidence.read`, the `derived/tasks` fields `repo, key, status, model, wall_s`); Assumption 11 (basenames); the `Generated-By` trailer convention of `tools/factory/seat/factory-brief` (`Generated-By: dsh … (seat headless, factory run <RUN>)` — this plan's shape `Generated-By: helm-home refresh / <model> (lane job <id>)`); HH1's `helm-home-unit` sandbox has `git` and the `pkgs/evidence` copy.

- [ ] **Step 1: red.** `tests/helm-home/test_refresh.py` and the two fixtures; red: `nix develop -c pytest tests/helm-home -q` → `ERROR tests/helm-home/test_refresh.py - FileNotFoundError: … pkgs/helm-home/refresh.py`. Paste.
- [ ] **Step 2: `refresh.py`.** Green: `pytest tests/helm-home -q`; `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.helm-home-unit -L --no-link`.
- [ ] **Step 3: the app's flow.** `nix run .#helm-home -- --self-check` still prints; `helm-home-package` green (the install check). The live flow is §Operator step 7c.
- [ ] **Step 4: lint, one commit.**

**Tests** (`test_refresh.py`; a fake `run` recording calls; a real temporary git repo for `accept`):

| # | assertion | discriminating fixture row | mutant |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `payload`: a 30-line git log → 20 lines requested (`-n 20` in the argv) and a 5,000-byte section → cut at 4,000 with `\n[cut]`; `bytes` is the sum | an over-long section | no cap → red; cap at 4,096 → the byte assertion red |
| 2 | `payload.checks`: 40 names → 30, sorted; `nix flake show` rc 1 → `no checks readable` | 40 names, a failing show | unsorted → red; raise on rc 1 → red |
| 3 | `payload.ledger`: a store with 12 `derived/tasks` rows for `repo == "media"` and 3 for another repo → the newest 10 media rows, each line exactly `ts key status model wall_s`, no other field | mixed repos, > 10 rows | filter dropped → 15 rows → red; a sixth field (`plan`) rendered → red |
