tasks.body:
**Why.** Decision 33a: the seat's bash tools only, driven by the graph runner; `dark-factory.js` archived. The file is load-bearing for three anchors (Assumption 5). After FA13 and FA14 the parity role `render.test.mjs` played is `factory-registry.py check`, and the graph check has no derivation running it. `docs/MAP.md`'s Checks section is asserted equal to the flake's check set (`flake.nix:1388-1391`); no check name changes, so only the map's file listing is regenerated. `flake.nix` → `platform`, `docs/MAP.md` → `evidence` (Assumption 16), hence three `areas:`. Assumption 22 applies.

**Files.**
- `git mv tools/factory/dark-factory.js tools/factory/archive/dark-factory.js`; `git mv tests/factory/render.test.mjs tools/factory/archive/render.test.mjs` — both the removed and the archived paths are in `touches` (G5 names files, not owners).
- Modify `flake.nix`: delete every line `grep -n 'dark-factory\|darkFactory' flake.nix` prints and the comment blocks they sit in (at HEAD `:74-76`, `:87-93`, `:102-103`, `:1342-1344`, `:1349`, `:1408-1411`, `:1426` — re-grep first; the lines move); in `factory-unit` also delete the `render.test.mjs` `cp` (`:1430`) and `node` line (`:1440`); add `cp` lines for `tools/factory/seat/factory-graph.py`, `factory-registry.py`, `factory-artifact.py`, `tools/factory/agents.toml`, `.claude/agents/`, and the graph block written so that zero graphs is a real no-op — at this task's landing none exists (`ls .claude/workflows/*.toml` → `No such file or directory`; FA19 and FA21 land later), and without `nullglob` the loop would `cp` the literal pattern and `factory-graph.py check` would exit 2 on `unreadable:`:
  ```
  mkdir -p .claude/workflows .claude/agents
  shopt -s nullglob
  graphs=( ${self}/.claude/workflows/*.toml )
  for f in "''${graphs[@]}"; do cp "$f" .claude/workflows/; done
  if [ "''${#graphs[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then python3 tools/factory/seat/factory-graph.py check .claude/workflows/*.toml; else echo "graphs: none"; fi
  python3 tools/factory/seat/factory-registry.py check && echo "registry: ok"
  ```
  (`''${` is Nix's escape for `${` inside an indented string.) `pkgs.python3` is already in the derivation's `nativeBuildInputs` (`flake.nix:1419-1422`).
- Modify `tests/lint/js-lint.sh`: delete the probe comment (`:16-20`), the two `_ARM` literals (`:21-22`), the arm-B branches (`:51`, `:61`, `:119-135`), the two report lines (`:165-166`) and the `:69` comment (`grep -n 'FORMATTER_ARM\|LINTER_ARM\|dark-factory\|darkFactory' tests/lint/js-lint.sh` → empty after).
- Modify `docs/MAP.md`: `nix develop -c python3 pkgs/evidence/repomap.py --root . write` (never by hand; `lint` diffs the Checks section, `flake.nix:1391`).

**Interfaces.**
1. `git ls-files tools/factory/dark-factory.js tests/factory/render.test.mjs` → empty; `git ls-files tools/factory/archive/` → both files.
2. `grep -c 'dark-factory' flake.nix tests/lint/js-lint.sh` → `0` for each.
3. `factory-unit` runs `factory-graph.py check` over every `.claude/workflows/*.toml` in the tree at build time — none at this task's landing, so the log reads `graphs: none` and the derivation is green until FA19/FA21 add one — and `factory-registry.py check` (live at once), failing the derivation on either's exit 2.
4. `plan.test.mjs` keeps running in `factory-unit` unchanged (it names `route.py` 0 times: `grep -c 'route.py' tests/factory/plan.test.mjs`).
5. No check name changes; `docs/MAP.md`'s `## Checks` list is unchanged.

**Steps.**
1. Red, in two parts. (i) Registry drift: append a blank line to `.claude/agents/review.md`, then `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.factory-unit -L --no-link` **before** the `flake.nix` edit → exit 0 (the gap); after the edit → `registry: review: drift`; `git checkout .claude/agents/review.md`. (ii) The archive: after the `git mv`, `factory-unit` and `lint` before the `flake.nix` edit → both fail (`cp: cannot stat '…/dark-factory.js'`; `error: getting status of '…/dark-factory.js'`). Paste all four outputs.
2. `git mv` both files; `git add tools/factory/archive`.
3. `flake.nix` edits per Files; `nix develop -c nixfmt --check flake.nix` (or the formatter `lint` runs: `grep -n 'nixfmt\|alejandra' flake.nix | head -2`) clean.
4. `js-lint.sh` edit; `docs/MAP.md` regeneration.
5. Green: `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.factory-unit -L --no-link`, `.#checks.x86_64-linux.lint`, `.#checks.x86_64-linux.unit` → all exit 0; the `factory-unit` log shows `graphs: none` and `registry: ok`. Paste.
6. Mutants:
   - **M1 registry-check-absent**: delete the `factory-registry.py check` line → step 1(i)'s drifted shim builds green (`status 0`) — the red is the killer, re-run it.
   - **M2 graph-check-absent**: delete the graph loop → with a fixture `.claude/workflows/bad.toml` (dangling edge) added to the workspace, `factory-unit` builds green; with the line, it fails `graph … dangling edge`. Remove the fixture after.
   - **M5 empty-glob-unguarded**: drop `shopt -s nullglob` and the count test → with the workspace's `.claude/workflows/` holding no `.toml` (the tree at this landing), `factory-unit` fails on `cp: cannot stat '…/*.toml'` or `graph …/*.toml: unreadable:`; with the guard it is green — the log line `graphs: none` is the witness.
   - **M3 archive-copied**: re-add `cp ${self}/tools/factory/archive/dark-factory.js …` and the `node --check` → Interface 2's `grep -c` is 2 — the probe `no-dark-factory-in-flake` fails.
   - **M4 map-stale**: leave `tools/factory/dark-factory.js` in `docs/MAP.md` → `grep -c 'tools/factory/dark-factory.js' docs/MAP.md` → 1, the probe fails.
7. Negative control: `plan.test.mjs` still runs and passes inside `factory-unit` (`grep -c 'plan.test.mjs' flake.nix` → 2: the `cp` and the `node`). Mutant: delete an `assert` from `plan.test.mjs`'s copy in the sandbox — not possible without touching the file, so instead temporarily point the `cp` at a fixture that `throw`s → `factory-unit` fails; revert. This proves the derivation still executes the test rather than merely copying it.
8. One commit, subject above; body cites `4d5266d` as the archived file's last commit.

**Tests** (assertion → mutant; fixture → discriminating row): registry check live in `factory-unit` → M1; graph check live → M2; zero graphs is a no-op → M5 (fixture: the empty workflows directory of this landing); `dark-factory` gone from the flake → M3; map regenerated → M4; fixture `plan.test.mjs` still executed → the throwing fixture.

**probes:**

tasks.body:
**Why.** Decision 37a fixes the shape — `patches/<pkg>/NNNN-*.patch` applied in `postPatch` — and nothing of it exists: `ls patches lib/patchSeries.nix` → `No such file or directory` (A4); `self.lib` exports `mkAgent` and `checkHelmDeclaration` only (A6). Every vendored upstream (38b) needs the same hook, so it is written once here with its refusals proven; each consumer (PL3's `claude-code` first) is a one-line call.

**Files.**
- Create `lib/patchSeries.nix` — `{ lib }: rec { readSeries = dir: …; renderPostPatch = dir: …; applySeries = dir: pkg: …; }` — exactly three exports (Interfaces 1–4); `applyTo` is not among them because it needs the flake's `self`. Header `{ lib }:` is a real argument, not `{ ... }:` (G10).
- Modify `flake.nix`: in `lib = { … }` (`:1036-1042`) add one binding, `patchSeries = let ps = import ./lib/patchSeries.nix { inherit (nixpkgs) lib; }; in ps // { applyTo = name: ps.applySeries (self + "/patches/" + name); };` — `self.lib.patchSeries` then carries four names (the probe); in `checks.${system}` (before `:3205`) add `patch-series-eval` and `patch-series-negative`, both from `import ./tests/integration/patch-series.nix { inherit pkgs; inherit (nixpkgs) lib; patchSeries = self.lib.patchSeries; }`.
- Create `patches/README.md` — the on-disk contract (Interfaces 1–3 in prose), the `applyTo` call, the pointer to `EV6`'s ledger.
- Create `tests/integration/patch-series.nix` — `{ pkgs, lib, patchSeries }: { eval = …; negative = …; }` holding the fixture derivations and the two checks' bodies.
- Create the thirteen fixture files: `src/hello.txt` = `hello\n`; `good/0001-first.patch` rewrites `hello` → `hello, world`; `good/0002-second.patch` appends `second` **with `hello, world` as its context line** so it applies only after 0001; `bad-dup/` two patches both numbered `0001`; `bad-apply/0001-does-not-apply.patch` a hunk whose context is `goodbye`; `bad-stray/` a valid 0001 plus `notes.txt`; `empty/` holds `README.md` alone (Interface 4's guard). Each `README.md` is one line naming what the directory proves; patches come from `diff -u` (Step 2), never hand-typed.

**Interfaces.**
1. `readSeries dir` returns the paths of `dir`'s regular files matching `^[0-9]{4}-.*\.patch$`, sorted by name (zero-padded numbers sort numerically).
2. It throws `patchSeries: <dir>: duplicate number NNNN (<a>, <b>)` if two files share a number, and `patchSeries: <dir>: stray file <name> (only NNNN-*.patch and README.md are allowed)` for any other entry, including a subdirectory. An empty directory or one holding only `README.md` returns `[ ]`.
3. `renderPostPatch dir` is the shell text `patch -p1 --no-backup-if-mismatch < <store path>\n` per patch, in order, no `|| true` (a re-applied patch exits 1 with or without `--forward`, A30, so that flag is no rule here); a missing directory is an eval error (`builtins.readDir` on a non-existent path), so a typo in a package name fails eval, not silently at runtime.
4. `applySeries = dir: pkg: let s = readSeries dir; in if s == [ ] then pkg else pkg.overrideAttrs (old: { postPatch = (old.postPatch or "") + renderPostPatch dir; });` — an empty series returns `pkg` itself, so the store path is identical by construction (without the guard `postPatch = ""` would be a new attribute on a package that has none, A6, and the drv hash would change).
5. `self.lib.patchSeries.applyTo "<pkg>"` = `applySeries (self + "/patches/<pkg>")`, defined once in `flake.nix` (Files), the one call site consumers use.
6. `patch-series-eval` passes iff (a) the good series, applied to the fixture source through `applySeries`, yields exactly `hello, world\nsecond\n`, and (b) `applySeries ./empty src == src` (derivation equality is outPath equality), else it throws `patch-series-eval: an empty series changed the derivation`.
7. `patch-series-negative` passes iff (a) `builtins.tryEval (readSeries bad-dup)` → `success = false`, (b) the same for `bad-stray`, (c) the rendered `bad-apply` postPatch, run under `bash -eu` against a copy of `src`, exits non-zero with `Hunk #1 FAILED` or `can't find file to patch`, and (d) the rendered good postPatch under the same runner exits 0 — the control.

**Steps.**
1. **Red.** Write the thirteen fixtures and `tests/integration/patch-series.nix` first (they import `lib/patchSeries.nix`, which does not exist), add the two checks to `flake.nix`, `git add` everything, then `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.patch-series-eval -L --no-link` → `error: getting status of '/nix/store/…-source/lib/patchSeries.nix': No such file or directory`. Paste it. Then write a naive `lib/patchSeries.nix` whose `readSeries` returns every file (no filter, no refusal) and re-run `patch-series-negative` → `patch-series-negative: bad-stray was accepted` — the second red, pasted too.
2. Make the patches: `cd tests/fixtures/patch-series && cp -r src w && sed -i 's/hello/hello, world/' w/hello.txt && diff -u src/hello.txt w/hello.txt | sed 's,^--- src/,--- a/,;s,^+++ w/,+++ b/,' > good/0001-first.patch`; then `echo second >> w/hello.txt` and the same `diff` against the post-0001 copy for `0002-second.patch`; `bad-apply` from a source whose line reads `goodbye`; `rm -r w`. `bad-dup/0001-first.patch` is a copy of `good/0001-first.patch`; `bad-dup/0001-second.patch` a copy of `good/0002-second.patch`; `bad-stray/0001-first.patch` the same copy plus `echo x > bad-stray/notes.txt`.
3. Write the real `lib/patchSeries.nix` to Interfaces 1–4 (`builtins.readDir`, `lib.filterAttrs`, `builtins.match`, a `lib.foldl'` over numbers for the duplicate check, `lib.sort lib.lessThan` on names).
4. Write `patches/README.md` and `python3 pkgs/evidence/repomap.py --root . write` (two new checks, one new test file — A24).
5. **Green.** `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.{patch-series-eval,patch-series-negative,lint} -L --no-link` → exit 0, the negative log carrying `bad-dup refused`, `bad-stray refused`, `bad-apply failed as required: Hunk #1 FAILED at 1.`, `good applied under the same runner`. `nix eval --raw .#lib.patchSeries.readSeries --apply 'f: toString (f ./tests/fixtures/patch-series/good)'` → two store paths, 0001 before 0002.
6. **Mutants**, each applied, run, pasted, reverted (`git checkout lib/patchSeries.nix tests/`):
   - **M1 reverse-order** — sort with `lib.flip lib.lessThan`. Kill: `patch-series-eval` → `Hunk #1 FAILED` (0002's context needs 0001 first); the check fails at build.
   - **M2 swallow-failure** — append ` || true` in `renderPostPatch`. Kill: `patch-series-negative` → `patch-series-negative: bad-apply was accepted`, exit 1.
   - **M3 no-dup-check** — remove the duplicate `throw`. Kill: `patch-series-negative` → `patch-series-negative: bad-dup was accepted`.
   - **M4 allow-stray** — drop the stray-file `throw` (filter silently). Kill: `patch-series-negative` → `patch-series-negative: bad-stray was accepted`.
   - **M5 lose-old-postPatch** — set `postPatch = renderPostPatch dir` without `old.postPatch`. Kill: the eval fixture's source derivation carries `postPatch = "echo pre > marker"`, and the check asserts `marker` exists → `patch-series-eval: upstream postPatch was dropped`.
   - **M6 wrong-expected** (fixture control) — change the eval check's expected text to `hello\nsecond\n`. Kill: `patch-series-eval` → `patch-series-eval: got 'hello, world\nsecond\n', expected 'hello\nsecond\n'` — proves the assertion reads the real output.
   - **M7 drop-empty-guard** — remove the `if s == [ ] then pkg` branch. Kill: `patch-series-eval` → `patch-series-eval: an empty series changed the derivation` (Interface 6b on the committed `empty/` fixture; PL3's two `drvPath` lines would differ the same way).
7. **Negative control.** Interface 7(d): the good series under the negative check's own runner exits 0 — the runner can pass, so its failures mean something. Its discriminating row is M2's inverse: replace `bad-apply` with `good` in arm (c) → `patch-series-negative: bad-apply was accepted`, because the good series applies.
8. Commit (G6): both reds, the three greens, the `nix eval` order line, six mutant outputs, the control and its row, and the `repomap.py write` note in the body.

**Tests (assertion → mutant; fixture → discriminating row).** Interface 1 order → M1; 2 duplicate → M3; 2 stray → M4; 3 no `|| true` → M2; 4 preserves `old.postPatch` → M5; 4 empty guard → M7 (fixture `empty/`); 6a exact output → M6. Control fixture `good` under the negative runner → the arm-(c) swap.

**probes:**
- fixture-files: `git ls-files tests/fixtures/patch-series | wc -l` :: ge 13 :: the touches list
- fixture-files-exact: `git ls-files tests/fixtures/patch-series | wc -l` :: le 13 :: the touches list, exact count
- readme-only-dirs: `ls patches` :: eq README.md :: A4 — the tree carries no package series until PL3
- lib-exports: `nix eval --json .#lib.patchSeries --apply 'p: builtins.attrNames p'` :: eq ["applySeries","applyTo","readSeries","renderPostPatch"] :: Interfaces 1–5 — the flake overlay adds applyTo to the module's three

tasks.body:
**Why.** `coreSpecialArgs.claude-code-pkg = llm-agents.packages.x86_64-linux.claude-code` (`sed -n '938p' flake.nix`, A6) reaches the host unpatched — the first vendored upstream 38b names has no hook. And the flake carries a wrong fact: `sed -n '6p;12p' flake.nix` → the pin is `a5cc6f2c37bf…` while the comment says `ac62194c3917, 2026-01-02` (A7). 47a says a bump fails the build hard; today nothing builds the wired package as a check, so the failure would surface at `nixos-rebuild`, in the operator's hands (G1). `patch-series-apply` moves it to `nix build`.

**Files.**
- Modify `flake.nix`: (a) `:938` becomes `claude-code-pkg = self.lib.patchSeries.applyTo "claude-code" llm-agents.packages.x86_64-linux.claude-code;`; (b) the comment `:7-19` — `ac62194c3917, 2026-01-02` replaced by the lock's live rev and date (`nix flake metadata --json | jq -r '.locks.nodes."nixpkgs-host".locked | "\(.rev[0:12]), \(.lastModified | todate[0:10])"'`) and the `pnpmConfigHook` sentence re-verified in Step 3; (c) a new check `patch-series-apply` before `:3205`: `pkgs.runCommand "patch-series-apply" { } ''test -e ${coreSpecialArgs.claude-code-pkg}; touch $out''` — the one interpolation puts the wired package's drv in the check's `inputDrvs`, so building it forces that build and a non-applying patch fails here. (No per-patch `test -e` loop: a tracked patch file interpolated into a string is always realised, so such a line can never fail — erratum 11; the patch files already sit in the package's closure through the rendered `postPatch`.)
- Create `patches/claude-code/README.md` — upstream `numtide/llm-agents.nix` at the `:20` rev, "series empty as of PL3", the `applyTo` line, "a bump follows `docs/runbooks/upstream-bump.md` (PL7)".

**Interfaces.**
1. `coreSpecialArgs.claude-code-pkg` is `applyTo "claude-code"` over the upstream package: with an empty series it *is* the upstream derivation (PL2 Interface 4's guard), so `nix eval --raw .#nixosConfigurations.core.config.system.build.toplevel.drvPath` is unchanged by this task (paste before/after); with a non-empty series its `postPatch` ends with the rendered series. Until the first patch lands the wiring's permanent assertion is textual (probe `hook-wired`); its build-level proof is Step 1's temporary patch, re-run by every bump task's Step 1 (PL7).
2. `patch-series-apply`'s `inputDrvs` name the claude-code drv (probe `apply-check-depends` → 1 or more on the committed tree), so building the check builds the wired package, and a patch that no longer applies fails here before any switch.
3. The `:7-19` comment names the rev `flake.lock` records for `nixpkgs-host` and the reasoning holds at that rev: `pnpmConfigHook` is present or absent there, and the comment says which.
4. `patches/claude-code/` contains exactly `README.md` (Interface 2 of PL2 admits it).

**Steps.**
1. **Red.** Add the `patch-series-apply` check to `flake.nix` first, with a **temporary** `patches/claude-code/0001-red.patch` whose hunk targets `a/does-not-exist.txt`; `git add -A patches flake.nix`; `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.patch-series-apply -L --no-link` → `can't find file to patch at input line 3` … `error: builder for '/nix/store/…-claude-code-….drv' failed`. Paste it; `git rm` the temporary patch — it is not in `touches`, and the body says so.
2. Edit `:938` and write `patches/claude-code/README.md`.
3. Re-verify the comment's claim at the live pin: `nix eval --json github:NixOS/nixpkgs/$(nix flake metadata --json | jq -r '.locks.nodes."nixpkgs-host".locked.rev')#legacyPackages.x86_64-linux.pnpmConfigHook.name 2>&1 | tail -1` → either a name (the hook exists; the comment then says "kept unfollowed because llm-agents' own nixpkgs carries the unfree allowance and the rev its lock tested") or `error: attribute 'pnpmConfigHook' … missing` (the reason stands). Paste the line, rewrite `:7-19`; `grep -c ac62194c3917 flake.nix` → `0`.
4. `python3 pkgs/evidence/repomap.py --root . write` (one new check, A24).
5. **Green.** `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.patch-series-apply -L --no-link` → exit 0; `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.host-core -L --no-link` → exit 0; `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.lint -L --no-link` → exit 0; `nix eval --raw .#nixosConfigurations.core.config.system.build.toplevel.drvPath` → the same path as on the base commit (paste both).
6. **Mutants**, each applied, run, pasted, reverted:
   - **M1 unhooked** — revert `:938` to the bare `llm-agents…claude-code`. Kill: the `hook-wired` probe → `0` (green `1`); with Step 1's temporary patch restored, `patch-series-apply` builds green under M1 where the wired tree turns it red — both pasted. (With an empty series the two trees are eval-identical by Interface 1; the text-level kill is recorded as such.)
   - **M2 apply-check-blind** — remove `test -e ${coreSpecialArgs.claude-code-pkg}` from the check. Kill: `nix derivation show .#checks.x86_64-linux.patch-series-apply | jq -r '.[].inputDrvs | keys[]' | grep -c claude-code` → `0` (green ≥ 1) — permanent, on the committed tree, no temporary patch needed (erratum 24); the Step 1 patch turning green under M2 is pasted as the second witness.
   - **M3 stale-comment** — restore `ac62194c3917`. Kill: `grep -c ac62194c3917 flake.nix` → `1` (green `0`); this is a fact assertion, killed by the probe below.
   - **M4 stray-in-series** — add `patches/claude-code/notes.txt`. Kill: `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.host-core` → `patchSeries: …/patches/claude-code: stray file notes.txt …` (PL2's refusal reaches the host eval through Interface 1).
7. **Negative control.** `host-core` and `patch-series-apply` pass with the empty series and the store path is unchanged (Step 5) — the hook is a no-op when there is nothing to apply. Discriminating row: Step 1's temporary patch turns `patch-series-apply` red while `host-core` stays green (eval does not build), which is exactly why the check exists.
8. Commit (G6) with the red, the Step 3 line, the greens, the two `drvPath` lines, four mutant outputs and the control row.

**Tests (assertion → mutant; fixture → discriminating row).** Interface 1 → M1 (probe `hook-wired`); 2 → M2 (probe `apply-check-depends`); 3 → M3; 4 → M4. Control: empty series, unchanged `drvPath` → Step 1's temporary patch.

**probes:**
- stale-rev-gone: `grep -c ac62194c3917 flake.nix || true` :: le 0 :: A7
- series-dir: `ls patches/claude-code` :: eq README.md :: Interface 4
- comment-names-lock-rev: `test "$(nix flake metadata --json | jq -r '.locks.nodes."nixpkgs-host".locked.rev[0:12]')" = "$(sed -n '7,19p' flake.nix | grep -oE '[0-9a-f]{12}' | head -1)" && echo same` :: eq same :: Interface 3

tasks.body:
**Why.** 39b asks for a view of "the patches the next switch carries and the generation each landed in". The generation half is Helm's (increment 3); the half only the closure can answer — which patches were *built in* — has no source today: `grep -rn 'patches' hosts/core/*.nix` → no match; `ls /etc/helm` → `config.json`, `profile` (A23). `environment.etc."helm/profile"` (`hosts/core/default.nix:40`) is the house model: a fact about the built system, rendered at eval time, readable at runtime. Q3(a) keeps this task.

**Files.**
- Create `hosts/core/patches.nix` — verbatim: `{ lib, ... }: let patchSeries = import ../../lib/patchSeries.nix { inherit lib; }; root = ../../patches; names = lib.attrNames (lib.filterAttrs (_: t: t == "directory") (builtins.readDir root)); in { environment.etc."helm/patches.json".text = builtins.toJSON (lib.genAttrs names (n: map (p: { file = baseNameOf p; sha256 = builtins.hashFile "sha256" p; }) (patchSeries.readSeries (root + "/${n}")))); }` — every directory under `patches/` is a series (PL2 Interface 2 admits an empty one).
- Modify `hosts/core/default.nix`: add `./patches.nix` to `imports` after `./seat.nix` (`:13`, A23).
- Modify `flake.nix`: a new check `core-patches-wiring` before `:3205`, in the `core-gaming-wiring` model (A9), verbatim: `core-patches-wiring = let coreCfg = self.nixosConfigurations.core.config; lib' = nixpkgs.lib; root = ./patches; names = lib'.attrNames (lib'.filterAttrs (_: t: t == "directory") (builtins.readDir root)); fromTree = lib'.genAttrs names (n: map (p: { file = baseNameOf p; sha256 = builtins.hashFile "sha256" p; }) (self.lib.patchSeries.readSeries (root + "/${n}"))); rendered = builtins.fromJSON coreCfg.environment.etc."helm/patches.json".text; mutated = fromTree // { "claude-code" = (fromTree."claude-code" or [ ]) ++ [ { file = "9999-mutant.patch"; sha256 = "0"; } ]; }; verdicts = map (b: rendered != b) [ fromTree mutated ]; in if !(coreCfg.environment.etc ? "helm/patches.json") then throw "core-patches-wiring: /etc/helm/patches.json is not rendered" else if !(builtins.elemAt verdicts 1) then throw "core-patches-wiring: the comparison arm is blind" else if builtins.elemAt verdicts 0 then throw "core-patches-wiring: /etc/helm/patches.json disagrees with patches/ (${builtins.toJSON rendered} vs ${builtins.toJSON fromTree})" else if !(rendered ? "claude-code") then throw "core-patches-wiring: claude-code is wired (PL3) but missing from /etc/helm/patches.json" else pkgs.runCommand "core-patches-wiring-check" { } "touch $out";`. The `names`/`fromTree` bindings duplicate `patches.nix`'s on purpose — a shared function would let M3 mutate both sides at once (erratum 3). `mutated` is the check's self-test: one comparison expression judges the real tree and a deliberately wrong one, so a blind comparison throws with no temporary patch (erratum 24).

**Interfaces.**
1. `/etc/helm/patches.json` is a JSON object with one key per directory under `patches/` (`README.md` at the top level is not a directory and is skipped); each value is an array, in series order, of `{ "file": "NNNN-name.patch", "sha256": "<64 hex>" }`.
2. An empty series renders `[]`, so after PL3 the file reads `{"claude-code":[]}` exactly (`builtins.toJSON` prints no whitespace).
3. The rendering shares `readSeries` with the build hook, so a directory the hook refuses (duplicate, stray) fails host eval with PL2's message rather than rendering a list the build never applied.
4. `core-patches-wiring` throws if the entry is missing, if its comparison cannot tell the rendered object from a deliberately mutated tree (`the comparison arm is blind`), if the rendered object differs from the tree's, or if `claude-code` — wired by PL3 — has no key; otherwise it is a trivial derivation.
5. Nothing reads the file yet (Helm's view is increment 3); it is world-readable like `/etc/helm/profile`.

**Steps.**
1. **Red.** Add `core-patches-wiring` to `flake.nix` first; `git add flake.nix`; `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.core-patches-wiring -L --no-link` → expected `error: core-patches-wiring: /etc/helm/patches.json is not rendered`. Paste it.
2. Write `hosts/core/patches.nix`; add the import to `default.nix`.
3. `python3 pkgs/evidence/repomap.py --root . write` (one new check, one new host file — A24).
4. **Green.** `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.core-patches-wiring -L --no-link` → exit 0; `nix eval --raw .#nixosConfigurations.core.config.environment.etc.\"helm/patches.json\".text` → `{"claude-code":[]}`; `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.host-core -L --no-link` → exit 0; `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.lint -L --no-link` → exit 0.
5. **Mutants**, each applied, run, pasted, reverted:
   - **M1 unimported** — remove `./patches.nix` from `imports`. Kill: `core-patches-wiring` → `core-patches-wiring: /etc/helm/patches.json is not rendered`.
   - **M2 hardcoded-empty** — set `.text = ''{"claude-code":[]}''`. Kill: with a temporary `patches/claude-code/0001-tmp.patch` (a copy of `good/0001-first.patch`, `git add`ed, removed after) the check → `core-patches-wiring: /etc/helm/patches.json disagrees with patches/ ({"claude-code":[]} vs {"claude-code":[{"file":"0001-tmp.patch","sha256":"…"}]})`; paste the green tree's `nix eval` with it present as the positive case.
   - **M3 drop-hash** — render `{ file = …; }` only. Kill: the same temporary patch, `nix eval` → no `sha256` key; `core-patches-wiring` → `disagrees` (the flake-side expression carries the hash).
   - **M4 skip-claude-code** — filter `names` to exclude `claude-code`. Kill: `core-patches-wiring: claude-code is wired (PL3) but missing from /etc/helm/patches.json`.
   - **M5 check-blind** — replace `rendered != b` in `verdicts` with `false`. Kill: `core-patches-wiring` → `core-patches-wiring: the comparison arm is blind` — on the committed tree, no temporary patch.
6. **Negative control.** The green tree with the temporary patch present: `core-patches-wiring` exit 0 and `nix eval` renders one entry with a 64-hex hash — the check can pass on a non-empty series, so its `disagrees` throw discriminates. Row: M2 on that same tree.
7. Commit (G6) with the red, the greens, the `nix eval` outputs (empty and with the temporary patch), five mutant outputs, and a body note that the temporary patch was never committed (`git status --porcelain patches/` → empty before the commit).

**Tests (assertion → mutant; fixture → discriminating row).** Interface 1 shape → M3; 2 → the `nix eval` paste; 3 → PL2's M4 through host eval (re-run: `patches/claude-code/notes.txt` → `host-core` throws); 4 missing → M1, blind → M5 (the `mutated` self-test is its committed fixture), disagrees → M2, no claude-code → M4. Control: the temporary non-empty series → M2.

**probes:**
- etc-entry: `nix eval --raw .#nixosConfigurations.core.config.environment.etc.\"helm/patches.json\".text` :: eq {"claude-code":[]} :: Interface 2 after PL3
- imports-count: `sed -n '4,17p' hosts/core/default.nix | grep -c '^    \./'` :: ge 11 :: A23's ten ./ imports plus ./patches.nix
- imports-count-exact: `sed -n '4,17p' hosts/core/default.nix | grep -c '^    \./'` :: le 11 :: A23, exact count
- self-test-arm: `grep -c 'the comparison arm is blind' flake.nix || true` :: ge 1 :: Interface 4

tasks.body:
**Why.** The sibling is deployed by two hand-made symlinks (`## Cross-plan`, Seat/Harness), the one measured violation of invariant 4. It ships no flake — `git -C ~/flakes/dsh-harness ls-files | grep -cx 'flake\.\(nix\|lock\)'` → `0` (A20) — so there is nothing to re-declare and no second lock to delete (42a holds vacuously). What 35b's "build gate" can mean for a tree of 99 files, 79 under `skills/`, is a derivation on `nixpkgs-host` (43b) that fails when the catalog's invariants break: this task builds it over the landed subtree (Q6(b), Q8(a)). `touches` is `flake.nix` alone: the subtree's files are read, never edited (erratum 25).

**Base.** The seat's branch starts from main after the landing merge: `git log --oneline -1 --merges -- pkgs/dsh-harness` names it; `git tag -l 'absorbed/dsh-harness-*'` names the tag; `git ls-files pkgs/dsh-harness | wc -l` → 99 (re-measure; the head may have moved past `d1b5f85`, A8). If any is missing the seat stops with `FACTORY-RESULT status=failed`, note `landing not found` — the landing is the orchestrator's act, never the seat's.

**Files.**
- Modify `flake.nix`: (a) in the outer `let`, `pkgsHost = nixpkgs-host.legacyPackages.${system};` (`grep -c 'nixpkgs-host.legacyPackages' flake.nix` → `0` today) and `dshHarnessSrc = pkgsHost.runCommand "dsh-harness-src" { src = ./pkgs/dsh-harness; nativeBuildInputs = [ pkgsHost.gnugrep pkgsHost.findutils ]; } ''…''` (Interfaces 1–4); (b) `packages.${system}.dsh-harness-src = dshHarnessSrc;`; (c) one check `dsh-harness-eval` — the umbrella name the outline fixed — with three arms: (i) builds `dshHarnessSrc` and asserts Interfaces 1–4 from the output; (ii) and (iii) the negative arms — two mutated copies of the source, one with a `SKILL.md`'s `name:` line deleted, one with its `description:` line deleted — run through the same builder body (`dshHarnessBuilder`, a shell function of `src` the check also invokes on each copy) and asserted to exit non-zero with, respectively, Interface 2a's and 2b's message.

**Interfaces.**
1. `packages.x86_64-linux.dsh-harness-src` is a store path containing `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and `skills/<name>/…` copied verbatim from `pkgs/dsh-harness`, and **not** `archive/` (archived history, not payload — `README.md:9-24` lists the contents without it).
2. (a) Every `skills/*/SKILL.md` in the output has a `^name: ` line whose value equals its directory name; the builder fails with `dsh-harness: skills/<d>/SKILL.md: name '<n>' != directory '<d>'` or `…: missing name:` otherwise. (b) Every such file has a `^description: ` line; the builder fails with `dsh-harness: skills/<d>/SKILL.md: missing description:` otherwise — a separate loop with its own message (A20: 0 files lack either today).
3. No file under `skills/` contains the string `superpowers:` (the stripped cross-skill prefix, `README.md:12-14`); the builder fails with `dsh-harness: <file>: superpowers: prefix present` otherwise.
4. `skills/` holds exactly as many directories as `SKILL.md` files (17 at A20; the builder measures both and fails on a mismatch, printing both counts).
5. The derivation is built by `nixpkgs-host`'s `runCommand` — the proof for 43b is `nix eval --raw .#dsh-harness-src.stdenv.drvPath` equal to `nix eval --raw --impure --expr '(builtins.getFlake "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/<nixpkgs-host rev>").legacyPackages.x86_64-linux.stdenv.drvPath'`.

**Steps.**

Paste both.

Kill: `dsh-harness-eval` → `dsh-harness-eval: a SKILL.md without description: was accepted` (arm iii), while arm ii still prints `refused as required: … missing name:` — the two halves of Interface 2 are proven apart (erratum 10).

tasks.body:
**Why.** 47a says a bump fails the build hard and "the bump is a task whose acceptance is a re-port of every patch"; the charter (`:222-224`) asks the Platform spec to set the cadence. Neither the procedure nor the cadence is written anywhere: `ls docs/runbooks | wc -l` → 13 (2026-09-14; the fill's 14 was wrong, erratum 15), and `ls docs/runbooks | grep -c -i 'bump\|pin\|upstream'` → `0`. The next `llm-agents` or `dsh` bump would be improvised against `flake.nix:7-19`'s reasoning, which PL3 has just had to correct once.

**Files.**
- Create `docs/runbooks/upstream-bump.md` — sections: `## When` (the cadence, A26 as assumed: a bump only when a typed task needs an upstream change, at most one per increment; one paragraph the seat rewrites if the operator vetoes A26 for (b) or (c)); `## The task's shape` (a typed `PL` task per bump: `touches` = `flake.lock`, `patches/<pkg>/*`, and `flake.nix` only if the `inputs` line changes; `acceptance` = `patch-series-apply, patch-series-eval, host-core, lint` plus `core-patches-wiring` and the package's own checks; the commit-subject grammar); `## Procedure` (`nix flake lock --update-input <input>`; `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.patch-series-apply -L --no-link` — red if any patch no longer applies, and that red *is* the bump task's Step 1; per failing patch, re-port with `diff -u` against the new upstream source, keeping its number; the re-port changes `/etc/helm/patches.json`'s sha256 values, so `core-patches-wiring` is re-run); `## What must not happen` (no `|| true`, no deleting a patch to make the build pass without a row in `docs/ledger/patches.toml` — `EV6`); `## Rollback` (`git checkout flake.lock` before the commit; after landing, a plain revert; the closure changes only at the operator's switch, G1).

**Interfaces.**
1. Every check name the runbook lists exists in `flake.nix` at the time of writing: `for c in $(grep -oE 'patch-series-[a-z]+|core-patches-wiring|host-core' docs/runbooks/upstream-bump.md | sort -u); do grep -q "^        $c =" flake.nix || echo "$c MISSING"; done` → no output. (PL7 sits beside PL4; if PL4 has not landed when PL7 runs, the seat confirms `grep -c '^        core-patches-wiring =' flake.nix` first and names that check as "once PL4 lands" — the loop must still print nothing.)
2. The cadence is one paragraph under `## When`, naming the assumption it follows (A26) and the plan.
3. The failure a non-applying patch prints is reproduced verbatim (`Hunk #1 FAILED`, `can't find file to patch`) so an operator can grep the build log for it.
4. `lint` stays green with the file present: `treefmt` has no Markdown formatter (`grep -c markdown treefmt.toml` → `0`) and `repomap.py` does not index runbooks, so the check's bearing here is G5's exact `touches` and the board block's currency — the body says so.

**Steps.**
1. **Red.** `test -e docs/runbooks/upstream-bump.md || echo missing` → `missing`; `grep -rl 'upstream-bump' docs/ | wc -l` → `0` — both pasted. Then a content red: write the file with `patch-series-applies` (a typo) in the task-shape list, run Interface 1's loop → `patch-series-applies MISSING`; paste it and fix the name.
2. Write the runbook to **Files**.
3. **Green.** Interface 1's loop → no output; `grep -c '^## When' docs/runbooks/upstream-bump.md` → `1`; `grep -c 'Hunk #1 FAILED' docs/runbooks/upstream-bump.md` → `1` or more; `grep -n '|| true' docs/runbooks/upstream-bump.md` → exactly one line, under `## What must not happen`; `git add docs/runbooks/upstream-bump.md; nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.lint -L --no-link` → exit 0.
4. **Mutants**, each applied, run, pasted, reverted:
   - **M1 forget-apply-check** — remove `patch-series-apply` from the task-shape list. Kill: `grep -c 'patch-series-apply' docs/runbooks/upstream-bump.md` → `1` (the Procedure mention alone; green `2` or more) — the seat pastes the green count first so the drop is visible.
   - **M2 stale-check-name** — write `patch-series-applies`. Kill: Interface 1's loop → `patch-series-applies MISSING`.
   - **M3 soften-hard-fail** — add "add `|| true` to unblock" under `## Procedure`. Kill: `grep -c '|| true' docs/runbooks/upstream-bump.md` → `2` (green `1`).
   - **M4 no-cadence** — delete the `## When` section. Kill: `grep -c '^## When'` → `0`.
5. **Negative control.** An existing runbook passes the same name loop: `for c in $(grep -oE 'core-backup-wiring|proton-backup-eval' docs/runbooks/backup.md | sort -u); do grep -q "^        $c =" flake.nix || echo "$c MISSING"; done` → no output (paste the `sort -u` list first; if empty, the seat uses `docs/runbooks/helm.md` with `helm-[a-z-]+`). Discriminating row: M2 on the new file.
6. Commit (G6) with the reds, the greens and four mutant outputs.

**Tests (assertion → mutant; fixture → discriminating row).** Interface 1 → M1, M2; 2 → M4; 3 → the `Hunk #1` grep (green paste); "no softening" → M3. Control: `backup.md` under the name loop → M2.

**probes:**
- check-names-exist: `for c in $(grep -oE 'patch-series-[a-z]+|core-patches-wiring|host-core' docs/runbooks/upstream-bump.md | sort -u); do grep -q "^        $c =" flake.nix || echo "$c MISSING"; done | wc -l` :: le 0 :: Interface 1
- when-section: `grep -c '^## When' docs/runbooks/upstream-bump.md || true` :: ge 1 :: Interface 2
- runbook-count: `ls docs/runbooks | wc -l` :: ge 14 :: 13 measured on 2026-09-14 plus this file

**Files:**
- Create: `tools/codex_limits.py`, `tests/test_codex_limits.py`

**Interfaces:**

`tools/codex_limits.py <path> [<path> ...]` (stdlib only — `json`, `sys`, `pathlib`; never a default path under `~/.codex`). Every internal failure named:

- **Zero argv paths:** `usage: codex_limits.py <path> [<path> ...]` to stderr, exit 2, before opening anything (Z5).
- **A nonexistent path:** `codex_limits: <path>: No such file or directory` to stderr, exit 2 immediately; earlier flushed rows stay printed (Z7, Z9).
- **Per path, in argv order:** buffer its `rate_limits` rows. Session, once per file: (1) the first `session_meta`'s `payload.id`; (2) else the `<uuid>` from `rollout-<ts>-<uuid>.jsonl`; (3) else the filename's own stem (`pathlib.Path(path).stem`) — `mixed.jsonl` → `"mixed"` — never the literal `unknown` (Z8).
- **Not valid JSON, or zero valid lines:** "not JSONL" — `codex_limits: <path> is not JSONL` to stderr, exit 2, nothing flushed for this file (Z2).
- **A `"type" == "rate_limits"` line** (the only kind kept, others skipped): `payload` must carry all four of `limit_id`, `used_percent`, `window_minutes`, `resets_at`; missing one — `codex_limits: <path> is missing "<key>" on a rate_limits record`, exit 2, nothing flushed, no further path processed (Z6).
- **Emitted row:** six keys, in order — `ts`, `session`, then `limit_id`/`used_percent`/`window_minutes`/`resets_at` verbatim from `payload` — nothing else reaches stdout (Z4).
- **Ordering (flush-then-continue, not all-or-nothing):** a clean path's rows flush before the next opens; a later failure does not un-print earlier ones; all clean → exit 0, rows grouped by path in argv order (Z9).

`checks.unit = pkgs.runCommand "openai-lab-unit" { nativeBuildInputs = [ python3 python3Packages.pytest ]; } ''cp -r ${self} src && chmod -R u+w src && cd src && pytest tests/test_codex_limits.py -q && touch "$out"'';` — no `|| true`; `set -e` fails the build on a failing `pytest` (Z10).

**Facts:** Assumption 7 (the rollout kinds, the spend gap, the board naming this task); `factory-codex-usage.py`'s idiom (`except (JSONDecodeError, ValueError, RecursionError): continue`) is a DIFFERENT contract (skip-and-continue vs. exit 2) — named so a task session never copies it by mistake. Shape stays UNMEASURED beyond the spike's named fields (D1); Operator item 3 supplies the first real path.

| Z2 | one good line then a truncated line → exit 2, one stderr line, NOTHING on stdout | that fixture | `continue` per-line instead of buffering-per-file → the good line reaches stdout, exit 0 → red |
| Z3 | two argv paths process independently: file A's `session` never carries into file B's rows | two files, differing `session_meta` ids | read `session` once from `argv[1]` only, reuse for every path → red |
| Z4 | no key beyond the six ever reaches stdout | a `rate_limits` record with an extra `"raw": {...}` key | build via `**record["payload"]` instead of the six named keys → `"raw"` leaks → red |

| Z9 | two-path ordering: (a) both clean → exit 0, A's rows before B's; (b) A clean, B not JSONL → A's row ALREADY on stdout before B's exit-2 stderr line | (a) two clean files; (b) one clean, one bad | (a) reverse/interleave argv → red; (b) buffer globally, flush only at the end → A's row lost → red |
| Z10 | `checks.unit` itself fails non-zero, pytest's failure in the log, when a fixture assertion is broken | any Z-row's expected value changed | add `\|\| true` after `pytest` in `checks.unit` → the same break leaves exit 0 → red (a survivor a bare `pytest -q` can't show); revert before Step 3 |

tasks.body:
Gate `docs/reviews/2026-09-08-opus-review-ol2-OL2.md` — REJECTED on two MAJORs (`plan_defect: wrong-fact`, secondary `underspecified`), both the plan's fault, not the seat's: OL2's Interfaces pinned a record shape — top-level `"type" == "rate_limits"`, a flat four-field payload — that does not exist in any real Codex rollout. Measured at the gate across `~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl`, 242 files: **0** top-level `rate_limits` records, **2,569** nested ones, every single one an `event_msg` record whose `payload.type == "token_count"` carries a `payload.rate_limits` object with exactly nine keys — `credits`, `individual_limit`, `limit_id`, `limit_name`, `plan_type`, `primary`, `rate_limit_reached_type`, `secondary`, `spend_control_reached` — and whose `used_percent`/`window_minutes`/`resets_at` live one level deeper still, inside `primary` and (when non-null) `secondary`. `limit_id` is a *plan* id (e.g. `"codex"`), not a window name — the old contract had no window discriminator and cannot express one record without inventing one. Against the operator's named rollout the delivered tool produced `EXIT=0`, zero stdout lines, empty stderr: a silent, contract-correct "success" indistinguishable from an idle session (MAJOR-1). Because the shape differs and the fixtures were never corrected, the gap claim `codex-rate-limits-shape-unmeasured` did not close (MAJOR-2) — its `closes_by` text lives in the plan's Dispatch section, which a seat's brief never includes, so OL2's seat had no way to see it. The seat's own conduct was exemplary throughout: 16/16 mutants dead, red-before-green reproduced, `unit`/`lint`/`nix flake check` green on `--rebuild`, touches exact, subject byte-identical, and it measured the mismatch unprompted and wrote it into its own module docstring rather than let green synthetic tests hide it. Nothing here is a correction of the seat's work; it is a re-spec of the contract the seat was correctly held to.

**This is a re-spec, not a patch** (the review's own recommendation): the CLI shape, the per-file atomicity, the flush-then-continue ordering and the whole test scaffold (subprocess-driven, `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory` fixtures, Z-row mutant discipline) carry forward unchanged in structure; the record-matching predicate, the required-key set, and the row shape are rewritten from measurement. Fresh workspace from main; `git fetch -q /home/dalhaka/factory/ws/ol2/OL2 task/OL2 && git cherry-pick -n FETCH_HEAD` carries OL2's commit `9db7f5b` as staged changes (`openai-lab` has no `docs/OPERATIONS.md`/`docs/MAP.md`, so neither conflict arm applies here). OL2's Interfaces items 1 ("stdlib only"), 2 (zero-argv usage), 3 (nonexistent path), 5 (not-JSONL / zero valid lines) and the `checks.unit` derivation (item 10) stand exactly as written and need no new test. Everything else changes.

**Files:**
- Modify: `tools/codex_limits.py`, `tests/test_codex_limits.py`

**Facts:** the closing condition for `docs/ledger/claims.toml`'s `codex-rate-limits-shape-unmeasured` gap claim, restated here because a seat's brief never includes the plan's Dispatch section where `closes_by` actually lives — **OL2b closes it by landing an extractor built on the measured key set above (the nine `rate_limits` keys; `used_percent`/`window_minutes`/`resets_at` nested under `primary` and `secondary`) that emits rows for the operator's named rollout, with the row count asserted by `checks.unit`.** §Global Constraints forbids fixturing from the real rollout file — every fixture here is hand-built JSONL matching the measured shape by *structure*, never copied from a real file's bytes. Two worked examples, both inventable outright, for the fixture builder to match (a made-up `resets_at`/`balance`/timestamp in each — no real session id, no real path):

(a null `secondary` — one row, window `"primary"`)

(a non-null `secondary` — two rows, windows `"primary"` and `"secondary"`)

**Interfaces:**

1. **The kept record kind (replaces item 6).** A record is kept only when `record.get("type") == "event_msg"` AND its `payload` is a dict with `payload.get("type") == "token_count"` AND `payload.get("rate_limits")` is a dict; everything else — `session_meta`, `turn_context`, `response_item`, `world_state`, any other `event_msg` payload type — is skipped, exactly as before.
2. **The rate_limits object's required keys (replaces item 7).** The kept object must carry all nine measured keys (Facts, above); missing one — `codex_limits: <path> is missing "<key>" on a rate_limits record`, exit 2, nothing flushed for this file, no further path processed.
3. **Each window, validated separately.** For each of `primary`, `secondary`: if its value is `None`, it contributes no row. If it is a dict, it must carry `used_percent`, `window_minutes`, `resets_at`; missing one — `codex_limits: <path> is missing "<key>" on a rate_limits <window> window` (`<window>` literally `primary` or `secondary`), exit 2, nothing flushed, no further path processed. Neither `None` nor a dict (a malformed record) is the same failure, same message. A record whose `primary` and `secondary` are both `None` is valid and simply contributes zero rows — not an error.
4. **Emitted row (replaces item 8).** Seven keys, in order: `ts`, `session`, `window`, `limit_id`, `used_percent`, `window_minutes`, `resets_at`. `window` is `"primary"` or `"secondary"`; `limit_id` is copied verbatim from the rate_limits object (a plan id, e.g. `"codex"` — no longer a window discriminator); `used_percent`/`window_minutes`/`resets_at` come from the window dict just validated. A `primary` and a non-null `secondary` on the same record each produce their own row, `primary` first. Nothing beyond these seven keys reaches stdout, from either the outer object or the window dict.
5. **Session resolution (replaces item 4, closes MINOR-1).** Per path: the first `session_meta` record whose `payload` is a dict AND contains `"id"` sets the session and stops the search — a `session_meta` with no `id` (or a non-dict `payload`) is skipped, not consumed, so a later `session_meta` that does carry an `id` is still reachable. Else the `<uuid>` of a `rollout-<ts>-<uuid>.jsonl` name. Else the stem. Never the literal `unknown`.
6. **A directory argument (closes MINOR-2).** `codex_limits: <path>: Is a directory`, stderr, exit 2, before opening any later path — the same failure class and shape as the existing "nonexistent path" arm (item 3), never an uncaught `IsADirectoryError` traceback. A `PermissionError` is out of scope for this round (untouched: still an uncaught traceback, unnamed by either gate).
7. **Silent-empty made observable (closes MAJOR-1).** After every path in argv has been processed with no fatal error, if the total number of rows emitted across *all* paths is zero, print `codex_limits: 0 rate_limits rows found across <n> path(s)` to stderr (`<n>` = the argv count) and exit **3** — never 0. If at least one row was emitted anywhere across the run, exit 0 as before (item 9's ordering and flush-then-continue are otherwise unchanged). This is the only new exit code; it never fires when any path errors (those keep their own exit-2 arms).

**Tests (assertion → mutant; fixture → discriminating row):**

| # | assertion | discriminating fixture | mutant / red |
|---|---|---|---|
| Z1 | mixing `session_meta`, `turn_context`, `event_msg`/`task_started`, `response_item` with one `event_msg`/`token_count` record carrying a null `secondary` and one carrying a non-null `secondary` yields exactly 3 rows (1 + 2), seven keys each, `window` correct on each | the mixed-kind fixture with the two worked examples above | drop the `payload.type == "token_count"` check → the `task_started` event_msg is read as a rate_limits carrier too → wrong count, red; keep the filter but emit `window` from `limit_id` instead of the loop variable → both rows show `window: "codex"`, red |
| Z2 | one good record then a truncated line → exit 2, one stderr line, nothing on stdout | a file with one valid record then `{"type":` | per-line `except (ValueError, RecursionError): continue` instead of raising → the good line reaches stdout, exit 0, red |
| Z3 | two argv paths process independently: file A's resolved session never carries into file B's rows | two files, each with its own valid `session_meta` | cache the first file's session module-wide and reuse it → red |
| Z4 | an extra unknown key inside the `rate_limits` object (e.g. `"raw": {...}`) is tolerated and never reaches the row; an extra key inside a window dict (e.g. `primary.extra`) is likewise dropped | the null-secondary worked example plus `"raw": {"synthetic": true}` on the outer object and `"extra": 1` inside `primary` | build the row via `**window, **{"limit_id": ...}` instead of the seven named keys → `"raw"` or `"extra"` leaks, red |
| Z5 | zero argv paths → usage line on stderr, exit 2, nothing on stdout | no arguments | drop the argv-length check → an `IndexError` traceback, red |
| Z6 | a `rate_limits` object missing `plan_type` → the one-line stderr naming the file and key, exit 2, nothing flushed, no further path processed | that object, key deleted, a second clean path after it | skip `plan_type` in the required-key loop → the second path is opened, red |
| Z7 | `primary` present but missing `resets_at` → `codex_limits: <path> is missing "resets_at" on a rate_limits primary window`, exit 2, nothing flushed, no further path processed | the null-secondary worked example, `resets_at` deleted from `primary` | validate the window dict with `.get(key)` defaulting to `None` instead of requiring the key → row emits `resets_at: null`, exit 0, red |
| Z8 | a record with `primary: null, secondary: null` contributes zero rows and is not an error; a sibling clean record elsewhere in the same file still emits its rows | one such record plus the null-secondary worked example in the same file | treat `primary is None` as a missing-key error → exit 2, red |
| Z9 | a nonexistent path → the documented stderr line, exit 2 | `tests/fixtures/does-not-exist.jsonl`-shaped tmp path | delete the `except FileNotFoundError` arm → uncaught traceback, red |
| Z10 | a directory path → `codex_limits: <path>: Is a directory`, exit 2, before any later path opens | `tmp_path.mkdir()`, plus a second clean path after it | catch only `FileNotFoundError` (today's code) → uncaught `IsADirectoryError` traceback, red |
| Z11 | no `session_meta` at all, filename `mixed.jsonl` → every row's session is `"mixed"`; a `rollout-<ts>-<uuid>.jsonl` name with no `session_meta` → session is the uuid | both filename shapes, no `session_meta` in either | fall back to the literal `"unknown"` instead of the stem/uuid, red |
| Z12 | MINOR-1: a file whose first `session_meta` has no `id` and whose second `session_meta` does → session resolves to the SECOND meta's id, not the stem | two `session_meta` records, first `{"type": "session_meta", "payload": {}}`, second carrying `"id"` | keep `found_session = True` on the first `session_meta` regardless of whether it yielded an id (today's code) → session falls back to the stem, red |
| Z13 | two-path ordering: (a) both clean, rows grouped A-then-B; (b) A clean, B not JSONL → A's rows are already on stdout before B's exit-2 stderr line, nothing further attempted | (a) two clean worked-example files; (b) one clean, one truncated | (a) reverse argv order before the print loop → red; (b) buffer every path's rows globally and flush once at the end → A's rows lost from the expected prefix, red |
| Z14 | MAJOR-1: every path processes cleanly but the total row count across all of them is zero → `codex_limits: 0 rate_limits rows found across <n> path(s)` on stderr, exit **3**, stdout empty; the same run with one matching record anywhere among the paths → exit 0 as before | (a) N clean files with no `event_msg`/`token_count` records at all; (b) the same plus one worked example inserted in the last file | drop the total-row-count check (today's code, extended to the new predicate) → exit 0 with empty stdout, indistinguishable from success, red |
| Z15 | `checks.unit` itself fails non-zero when a fixture assertion breaks (unchanged from OL2's Z10, re-verified against the new file) | any Z-row's expected value changed | add `\|\| true` after `pytest` in `checks.unit` → the same break leaves exit 0, red |

- [ ] **Step 1: The carried commit, then the tests.** Cherry-pick `9db7f5b` as staged changes. Write Z1–Z15 (Z2, Z5, Z9, Z15 keep OL2's originals nearly verbatim; every other test is new or materially rewritten for the nested shape) and run them red against the carried (flat-shape) implementation — `nix develop -c python3 -m pytest tests/test_codex_limits.py -q`, paste the failures.
- [ ] **Step 2: The edits** — rewrite `tools/codex_limits.py`'s record predicate, required-key validation, per-window validation, row assembly and the session_meta and directory handling (Interfaces 1–7); no change to `flake.nix`.
- [ ] **Step 3: Run green** — `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.unit -L --no-link`; `… lint`; `nix flake check -L` → `all checks passed!`.
- [ ] **Step 4: Mutants** — every row of the Tests table, one at a time, killing line pasted, file restored before the next.
- [ ] **Step 5: Commit** — one commit, subject below, `nix develop -c git commit -F <msgfile>`; trailers per Global Constraints; body pastes the Step-1 red, the Step-3 green, the mutant table, and states in one sentence that this landing closes `codex-rate-limits-shape-unmeasured`.

**Interfaces:**

`docs/runbook.md` carries exactly three `## ` headings, byte-exact (the prose beneath is free to reword — heading text and fenced commands are the contract):

- `## Bumping the pin` — one ` ```bash ` fence: `$ nix flake lock --update-input nixos-agent-env` then `$ nix flake check -L`.
- `## Dispatching a task` — states `factory-dispatch` cannot be used here (Assumption 9), then one fence: `$ FACTORY_SEAT=codex FACTORY_PLAN=<plan> setsid -f bash -c 'exec tools/factory/seat/factory-wave <run> /home/dalhaka/flakes/openai-lab "<KEY>" >> ~/factory/runs/<run>.wave.log 2>&1' </dev/null`.
- `## Where the gate record lives` — every review is committed in `~/nixos-agent-env`'s `docs/reviews/`, never the lab; one fence: `$ git -C ~/nixos-agent-env log -1 --format=%s -- docs/reviews`.

`flake.nix`'s `checks.unit` gains, after pytest: `[ "$(grep -c '^## ' docs/runbook.md)" = 3 ]`; one `grep -Fxq` per heading above; `bats tests/runbook.bats` (nativeBuildInputs gains `pkgs.bats`).

`tests/runbook.bats` extracts every `$ `-prefixed line inside a ` ```bash ` fence (`awk '/^```bash$/{f=1;next} /^```$/{f=0} f && /^\$ /{sub(/^\$ /,"");print}' docs/runbook.md`) and asserts each starts with a documented verb above — extracted commands, never surrounding prose.

**Facts:** the codex-arm plan's Dispatch section (launch-line shape; step 3, the review committed in `~/nixos-agent-env`); decision point 4; `factory-dispatch:104-108`; `~/flakes/codex`'s review lives at `docs/reviews/2026-09-07-opus-review-cx1b-CX1b.md`, not in `~/flakes/codex`. Z10 (OL2) proves `set -e` propagates, not repeated here.

| # | assertion | discriminating fixture | mutant / red |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | exactly 3 `## ` headings | with/without a stray fourth, or one deleted | add a fourth `## ` line → count 4 → red; delete one → count 2 → red |
| R2 | the three exact headings, each its own `grep -Fxq` | each heading present, reworded, or deleted in turn | reword `## Bumping the pin` → red; delete `## Dispatching a task` or `## Where the gate record lives` → red |
| R3 | every fenced `$ ` command matches a documented verb | as in Interfaces | drop `-L` from `nix flake check -L` without updating the verb list → red; an undocumented new command → red |

- [ ] **Step 2: The edits** — `docs/runbook.md`, `tests/runbook.bats`, `flake.nix` (the five new `checks.unit` lines).
- [ ] **Step 3: Run green** — `nix build .#checks.x86_64-linux.unit -L --no-link` (pytest plus R1–R3); `… lint`; `nix flake check -L` → `all checks passed!`.
- [ ] **Step 4: Commit** — one commit, subject below, `nix develop -c git commit -F <msgfile>`; trailers per Global Constraints, run `ol2`.
